After the death of his father Duke Wei of Western Zhou, he set himself up at Gong, modern Gongyi in Henan, in 367 BCE with the backing of the states of Zhao and Han, splitting the last royal…

duke-mu-of-qin.s: Duke Mu of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 659 to 621 BCE and is often listed among the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn period. He employed able foreign ministers, helped Chong'er of Jin take power and expanded Qin westward over the Rong peoples.

duke-town.s: Duke Town, or Atakpa, is one of the Efik settlements on the Calabar river in south-eastern Nigeria, founded with Creek Town and Old Town in the 17th century. Europeans called the towns together Old Calabar.

duke-wen-of-jin.s: Duke Wen of Jin, born Chong'er, spent nineteen years in exile among other states before taking the throne of Jin in 636 BCE. He invaded Cao in 632 BCE, defeated Chu at the Battle of Chengpu the same year and was recognised as hegemon, one of the Five Hegemons of the Spring and…

duke-wen-of-zhu.s: Duke Wen of Zhu was a ruler of the small state of Zhu, later known as Zou, in present-day Shandong. In 614 BCE he moved the capital to Yi after a divination warned that it would benefit the people but not the ruler, answering that a ruler's task was to benefit the people.

duke-xiang-of-song.s: Duke Xiang of Song ruled the State of Song from 650 to 637 BCE and sought to become hegemon of the Zhou states. At the Battle of Hong in 638 BCE he refused to attack the Chu army while it crossed the river or before it formed up, and was defeated and wounded.

dumbarton-rock.s: Dumbarton Rock is a volcanic plug on the north bank of the Clyde in western Scotland, known in Brittonic as Alt Clut, 'rock of the Clyde'. It was the chief fortress of the British kings of Strathclyde from at least the 5th century until Viking forces from Dublin besieged and…

dungarendra-singh.s: Dungarendra Singh was a Tomara ruler of Gwalior in the 15th century. He resisted attacks from neighbouring sultanates and patronised Jain communities, under whom the colossal Jain images were carved into the rock faces around Gwalior Fort, work continued by his son Kirti Singh.

duomi-khagan.s: Duomi Khagan, named Bazhuo, was the last khagan of the Xueyantuo on the Mongolian steppe. Succeeding his father Zhenzhu Khagan in 645 after killing his brother, he attacked Tang territory while Emperor Taizong campaigned in Korea.

durad-crnojevic.s: Đurađ Crnojević was the last lord of Zeta from the Crnojević family, ruling from 1490. He set up at Cetinje one of the earliest presses in the Balkans, which printed the Cyrillic Oktoih in 1494.

dutch-reformed-church.s: The Dutch Reformed Church was the main Calvinist church of the Netherlands and the established church of the Dutch Republic. It followed Dutch trade and settlement overseas, to the Caribbean, North America, the Cape Colony and Asia.

danish-west-india-and-guinea-company.n: Danish West India and Guinea Company
danish-west-india-and-guinea-company.s: The Danish West India and Guinea Company was a Danish chartered company founded in 1671 to run colonies in the Caribbean and trade on the Gold Coast of West Africa. It administered St Thomas, St John and, from 1733, St Croix, bought from France, as well as forts such as…

democritus.s: Democritus was a Greek philosopher from Abdera in Thrace, active in the later 5th and early 4th centuries BCE. Building on the ideas of his teacher Leucippus, he taught that everything consists of tiny, indivisible atoms moving in a void.

dumnorix.s: Dumnorix was a nobleman of the Aedui in Gaul and the brother of Diviciacus. He led the anti-Roman party among his people, married a Helvetian noblewoman and helped the Helvetii in their migration of 58 BCE.

donatism.s: Donatism was a Christian schism in Roman North Africa that began in 311 over the election of a bishop of Carthage. Its followers, named after Donatus, held that clergy who had handed over scriptures during the persecution of Diocletian had lost their authority.

dougga.s: Dougga, ancient Thugga, is an archaeological site in northern Tunisia. A Numidian town with a royal mausoleum, it became a prosperous Roman municipality with a capitol, theatre, temples and baths that are among the best preserved in North Africa.

dacians.s: The Dacians were an ancient people of the Carpathian region and the lower Danube, in what is now Romania and neighbouring lands, closely related to the Thracians and the Getae. Burebista united them in a powerful kingdom in the 1st century BCE, and under Decebalus they fought…

democratic-party-of-albania.s: The Democratic Party of Albania is a centre-right party founded in December 1990, the first opposition party allowed under the communist regime. Led by Sali Berisha, it won the 1992 elections, ending communist rule, and governed until the collapse of pyramid investment schemes…

demosthenes.s: Demosthenes was an Athenian statesman and the greatest orator of ancient Greece. In speeches such as the Olynthiacs and Philippics he urged Athens to resist Philip II of Macedon, and he helped build the alliance defeated at Chaeronea in 338 BCE.

demosthenes-general.s: Demosthenes was an Athenian general of the Peloponnesian War. In 426 BCE he defeated the Ambraciots at Olpae and Idomene in north-western Greece, and in 425 BCE he fortified Pylos, leading to the capture of Spartan troops on Sphacteria.

du-yu-king-of-shu.s: Du Yu, also known as Emperor Wang (Wangdi), is a legendary king of Shu who, according to later Chinese texts, taught his people agriculture. Tradition says he abdicated in favour of his minister Bieling, founder of the Kaiming dynasty, after Bieling controlled a great flood,…

demetrius-of-phalerum.s: Demetrius of Phalerum was an Athenian statesman and Peripatetic philosopher, a pupil of Theophrastus. Installed by Cassander, he governed Athens from 317 to 307 BCE, reforming its laws and limiting luxury, until Demetrius Poliorcetes expelled him.

dhatusena.s: Dhatusena was a king of the Anuradhapura Kingdom in Sri Lanka who reigned from about 455 to 473. He drove out South Indian rulers who had seized the north of the island, restored Buddhist institutions and built great irrigation works, above all the Kala Wewa reservoir.

dutugemunu.s: Dutugemunu was a Sinhalese king of the Anuradhapura Kingdom who reigned from about 161 to 137 BCE. Son of King Kavantissa of Ruhuna in the south of Sri Lanka, he defeated the Tamil ruler Elara and united the island under one king.

dirty-war.s: The Dirty War was the campaign of state terror waged by Argentina's military dictatorship between 1976 and 1983 against left-wing guerrillas, activists, students and other suspected opponents. Thousands were held in secret detention centres, tortured and killed, becoming the…

domingo-faustino-sarmiento.s: Domingo Faustino Sarmiento was an Argentine writer, educator and statesman who served as president from 1868 to 1874. An opponent of Rosas, he wrote Facundo in exile in Chile, a classic of Latin American literature contrasting civilisation and barbarism.

deyrulzafaran-monastery.s: Deyrulzafaran, the Monastery of Mor Hananyo, is a Syriac Orthodox monastery near Mardin in south-eastern Turkey. Built on an ancient site and refounded in the 8th century, it was the seat of the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch from the 12th century until 1932.

dagan.s: Dagon was a god worshipped in ancient Syria and Mesopotamia, attested from the 3rd millennium BCE at Ebla and Mari and associated with grain and fertility. The Bible presents him as the chief god of the Philistines, with temples at Ashdod and Gaza.

dakshinapatha.s: Dakshinapatha, the southern road, was the ancient Indian name for the trade route running from the Ganges plain south-west to the Deccan, and for the southern lands it reached. Mentioned in Buddhist texts, it linked cities such as Shravasti and Ujjain with Pratishthana on the…

draco-lawgiver.s: Draco was an Athenian legislator who about 621 BCE gave Athens its first written code of laws, replacing oral law and blood feud administered by the aristocracy. The laws were remembered for their severity, prescribing death for many offences, which gave rise to the word…

drina.s: The Drina is a river of the western Balkans, about 346 km long, formed by the Tara and Piva and flowing north into the Sava. For much of its course it marks the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia.

dezful.s: Dezful is a city in Khuzestan province, south-western Iran, on the Dez river at the foot of the Zagros mountains. It grew around an ancient bridge across the river, built in the Sasanian period, from which it takes its name.

daudpota.s: The Daudpota, or Daudpotra, are a tribe from Sindh whose chiefs claim descent from the Abbasid caliphs and therefore use the family name Abbasi. In the early 18th century a branch moved from upper Sindh to the Sutlej valley, where its leaders founded Bahawalpur and ruled the…

derawar-fort.s: Derawar Fort is a large square fortress in the Cholistan Desert of Pakistan's Punjab, south of Bahawalpur, whose forty massive bastions are visible from far across the desert. A fort was held there by Bhati Rajputs before the Abbasi nawabs of Bahawalpur took it in 1733 and…

dae-gwang-hyeon.s: Dae Gwang-hyeon was the crown prince of Balhae, a descendant of its founder Dae Joyeong, who led a large body of refugees to Goryeo after the Khitan Liao dynasty destroyed Balhae in 926. King Taejo of Goryeo welcomed him in 934, gave him the royal surname Wang and entered him…

da-monzon-diarra.s: Da Monzon Diarra was a king of the Bambara Empire of Ségou, ruling from 1808 to 1827, under whom the state reached the height of its power. He fought the Kaarta kingdom and the Fulani of Massina and dominated trade along the middle Niger.

drobeta-turnu-severin.s: Drobeta-Turnu Severin is a city in south-western Romania on the Danube, just below the Iron Gates gorge. On the site of the Roman town of Drobeta, where Apollodorus of Damascus built Trajan's bridge across the Danube in 105, a medieval fortress, Severin, was raised, and it was…

danube-swabians.s: The Danube Swabians are German-speaking people descended from settlers who moved into the Kingdom of Hungary, especially the Banat, Bačka and the region around Buda, after the Habsburg reconquest from the Ottomans in the 18th century. Many came from south-western Germany,…

dar-es-salaam.s: Dar es Salaam is the largest city and chief port of Tanzania, on the Indian Ocean coast. Founded in the 1860s by Sultan Majid of Zanzibar, it became the capital of German East Africa in 1891 and the starting point of the Central Railway to Lake Tanganyika.

dar-ul-funun.s: Dar ul-Funun was a college in Tehran opened in 1851 on the initiative of the Qajar chief minister Amir Kabir, the first modern institution of higher learning in Iran. Staffed at first largely by European teachers, it trained officers, doctors, engineers and officials in…

dahod.s: Dahod is a city in eastern Gujarat, India, near the borders of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, and the headquarters of Dahod district, created in 1997 from part of Panchmahal district. It lies on old trade routes between Gujarat and Malwa.

damaji-rao-gaekwad.s: Damaji Rao Gaekwad was a Maratha commander and ruler, son of Pilaji Rao Gaekwad, who led the family from 1732 to 1768. He took Baroda (Vadodara) and much of Mughal Gujarat, making the Gaekwads one of the great Maratha houses.

diwanus.s: Diwanus was a leader of the Bartians, one of the Old Prussian peoples, during the Great Prussian Uprising against the Teutonic Order that began in 1260. He led attacks on the Order's castles, including Bartenstein, and raided Chełmno Land.

deldo.s: Deldo was a king of the Bastarnae who led raids across the lower Danube into Thrace and Moesia. In 29 BCE the Roman governor of Macedonia, Marcus Licinius Crassus, defeated his army and killed him in single combat.

danteshwari.s: Danteshwari is a Hindu goddess, a form of Durga, worshipped as the patron deity of the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, India. Her main temple stands at Dantewada, at the meeting of the Shankhini and Dankini rivers, and is counted by tradition among the Shakti Pithas.

dantewada.s: Dantewada is a town in southern Chhattisgarh, India, the headquarters of Dantewada district, at the confluence of the Shankhini and Dankini rivers. It is named after the goddess Danteshwari, whose temple there was the shrine of the Rajas of Bastar.

dingane.s: Dingane was king of the Zulu from 1828 to 1840, after taking part in the assassination of his half-brother Shaka. In February 1838 he had the Voortrekker leader Piet Retief and his party killed, and his army was defeated by the Voortrekkers at Blood River in December 1838.

danebury.s: Danebury is an Iron Age hillfort in Hampshire, England, near Stockbridge. Excavated by Barry Cunliffe from 1969 to 1988, it is one of the most thoroughly studied hillforts in Britain.

doda-district.s: Doda district is an administrative district in the Chenab valley in the Jammu division of Jammu and Kashmir, India, with its headquarters at the town of Doda. Mountainous and largely rural, it includes the Bhadarwah valley.

deeg.s: Deeg is a town in eastern Rajasthan, India, north of Bharatpur. It was a stronghold of the Jat rulers of Bharatpur, fortified by Badan Singh in the early 18th century.

deshastha-brahmin.s: The Deshastha Brahmins are a Hindu Brahmin community of the Deccan plateau, the Desh, in Maharashtra and northern Karnataka. They supplied many of the administrators, accountants and scholars of the Deccan sultanates and the Maratha state, and several Maratha ministerial…

dorothea-of-montau.s: Dorothea of Montau was a mystic of Prussia. A married laywoman from Montau on the Vistula, after her husband's death she became an anchoress walled into a cell at the cathedral of Marienwerder in 1393, where she died a year later.

debal.s: Debal was a port of Sindh near the mouth of the Indus, close to modern Karachi, often identified with the excavated site of Banbhore. Active in Indian Ocean trade, it was the first city taken by Muhammad ibn Qasim in his conquest of Sindh in 711–712, after attacks on Arab…

diretas-ja.s: Diretas Já, 'Direct elections now', was a mass movement in Brazil in 1983–1984 demanding direct elections for president under the military dictatorship. Huge rallies in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and other cities drew millions, but Congress narrowly rejected the constitutional…

daesitiates.s: The Daesitiates were an Illyrian people of central Bosnia, in the hills around the upper Bosna valley. Under their leader Bato they began the Great Illyrian Revolt against Rome in 6 CE, joined by the Pannonian Breuci, and held out until 9 CE.

donoughmore-constitution.s: The Donoughmore Constitution was the constitution of British Ceylon from 1931 to 1947, based on the report of a commission led by the Earl of Donoughmore. It introduced universal adult suffrage, the first in Britain's Asian or African colonies, and a State Council whose…

diego-silang.s: Diego Silang was the leader of a revolt in the Ilocos region of northern Luzon against Spanish rule during the British occupation of Manila. Declaring himself a vassal of the British, he took Vigan in 1762, but he was assassinated in May 1763 by men in Spanish pay.

dara-shikoh.s: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son and favoured heir of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. A scholar and Sufi, he translated the Upanishads into Persian and wrote The Mingling of the Two Oceans on the common ground of Islam and Hinduism.

dongmyeong-of-buyeo.s: Dongmyeong is the legendary founder of Buyeo, an ancient kingdom of Manchuria. In the version recorded by Chinese writers from the 1st century CE, he was born to a servant woman of a northern kingdom after she was touched by a beam of sunlight, and escaped the king's pursuit…

drappes.s: Drappes was a Senonian leader in the last phase of Gallic resistance to Julius Caesar. In 51 BCE he gathered a band of fugitives and freed slaves and joined Lucterius of the Cadurci in holding the fortress of Uxellodunum.

dubnovellaunus.s: Dubnovellaunus was a British king of the late 1st century BCE and early 1st century CE known from coins issued in Kent and among the Trinovantes of Essex. He is probably the British king Dumnobellaunus who, according to the Res Gestae of Augustus, fled to the emperor as a…

diamantina.s: Diamantina is a colonial town in Minas Gerais, Brazil, formerly the Arraial do Tijuco. Diamonds were found there in the 1720s, and the Portuguese crown made the area a closed Diamond District under a royal monopoly.

duke-of-aveiro.s: Duke of Aveiro was a Portuguese ducal title created in 1535 for João de Lencastre, a grandson of King John II. The dukes were among the richest nobles of Portugal and held lands in Brazil, including the Captaincy of Porto Seguro.

deba-river.s: The Deba is a river of the Basque Country in northern Spain, flowing north through the province of Gipuzkoa past Arrasate-Mondragón and Eibar into the Bay of Biscay at the town of Deba. In the Iron Age and Roman period it is thought to have marked the boundary between the…

durance.s: The Durance is a river of south-eastern France, about 323 km long, rising in the Alps near Briançon and flowing south-west through Provence to join the Rhône near Avignon. Its valley has long been a route between the Alps and the Mediterranean, and in antiquity it bounded the…

damel.s: Damel was the title of the kings of Cayor, a Wolof kingdom on the coast of Senegal. The first Damel, Amari Ngoone Sobel Fall, threw off the authority of the Jolof Empire in 1549, and later holders were chosen from royal lineages by a council of electors.

douro.s: The Douro is one of the major rivers of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing about 897 km from the Sierra de Urbión in Soria westwards across northern Spain and Portugal to the Atlantic at Porto. In antiquity its basin was home to peoples such as the Vaccaei, Arevaci, Vettones and…

dunollie.s: Dunollie is a castle and early medieval fortress on a headland just north of Oban in Argyll, western Scotland. Irish annals record the burning of Dún Ollaigh in 686 and 698 and its destruction by Selbach in 701, when it was a chief seat of the Cenél Loairn kings of Dál Riata.

dunsterforce.s: Dunsterforce was a small Allied military mission of picked British and Dominion officers and troops under Major-General Lionel Dunsterville, sent through Persia in 1918 to organise resistance in the Caucasus after the collapse of the Russian army. It reached Baku in August…

dantidurga.s: Dantidurga was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, ruling in the northern Deccan from about 735 to 756. A feudatory of the Chalukyas of Badami, he overthrew his overlord Kirtivarman II around 753 and made the Rashtrakutas the leading power of the Deccan.

dhanga.s: Dhanga was king of the Chandela dynasty of Bundelkhand from about 950 to 999. Son of Yashovarman, he threw off the overlordship of the Gurjara-Pratiharas and made the Chandelas a leading power of northern India.

dhaka.s: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh, on the Buriganga river in the Ganges delta. Made the Mughal capital of Bengal by Islam Khan in 1610, it flourished on the muslin trade, and later became the capital of the province of Eastern Bengal and Assam from 1905 to…

dilwara-temples.s: The Dilwara Temples are a group of five Jain temples at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, India, famed for their intricately carved white marble interiors. The oldest, the Vimal Vasahi dedicated to Rishabhanatha, was built in 1031 by Vimala, a minister of the Chaulukya king Bhima I, and…

diophantus-general.s: Diophantus, son of Asclepiodorus, was a general from Sinope in the service of Mithridates VI of Pontus in the late 2nd century BCE. Sent to help Chersonesus Taurica against the Crimean Scythians of Palacus, he won several campaigns in about 110–107 BCE and then crushed the…

dards.s: The Dards are the peoples of the mountains of north-west Kashmir and northern Pakistan, including Gilgit, Chitral and Kohistan, who speak Dardic languages such as Shina and Khowar. Their name, found in ancient Sanskrit and Greek sources as Daradas and Derdai, was revived by…

dugdamme.s: Dugdamme was a king of the Cimmerians in the 7th century BCE, known from Assyrian texts and called Lygdamis by Greek writers. He led raids across Anatolia, sacking Sardis and, according to Greek tradition, burning the temple of Artemis at Ephesus, and threatened Assyria under…

djibo-bakary.s: Djibo Bakary was a Nigerien trade unionist and politician who led the Sawaba party. As head of the territorial government of Niger from 1957, he campaigned for a 'no' vote in the 1958 referendum on the French Community, seeking immediate independence.

douglas-treaties.s: The Douglas Treaties were fourteen land purchase agreements made between 1850 and 1854 by James Douglas, chief factor of the Hudson's Bay Company and governor of Vancouver Island, with First Nations around Victoria, Saanich, Sooke, Nanaimo and Fort Rupert. In return for…

dominica-freedom-party.s: The Dominica Freedom Party is a political party in Dominica, founded in 1968 and led for many years by Eugenia Charles. It won the 1980 election after the fall of Patrick John's government and governed until 1995, with Charles as the Caribbean's first woman prime minister.

duncansby-head.s: Duncansby Head is the most north-easterly point of mainland Great Britain, a headland near John o' Groats in Caithness, Scotland. Its sandstone cliffs, topped by a lighthouse, look over the Pentland Firth towards Orkney.

dunnet-head.s: Dunnet Head is a peninsula in Caithness, Scotland, whose cliffs form the most northerly point of mainland Great Britain. It looks across the Pentland Firth to the Orkney island of Hoy.

dardanus.s: In Greek mythology Dardanus was a son of Zeus and Electra, the founder of Dardania in the Troad and ancestor of the kings of Troy. Greek writers said he came to Asia from Arcadia or Samothrace, while an Italian tradition, followed by Virgil, made him a native of the Etruscan…

dniester.s: The Dniester is a river of Eastern Europe, about 1,360 kilometres long, rising in the Carpathians of western Ukraine and flowing through Moldova to the Black Sea near Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi. Known to the Greeks as the Tyras, it ran through the lands of many ancient peoples and…

diego-rodriguez-porcelos.s: Diego Rodríguez Porcelos was count of Castile from about 873 to 885, son of Count Rodrigo, under the kings of Asturias. On the orders of Alfonso III he founded Burgos in 884 as a fortified frontier post against the Emirate of Córdoba, extending Castilian settlement southwards.

dummer.s: The Dümmer is a shallow lake in Lower Saxony, Germany, near Diepholz, the second-largest lake in the state. Surrounded by moors and wet meadows and fed and drained by the Hunte river, it is an important reserve for water birds.

dornbirn.s: Dornbirn is the largest town in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, lying in the Rhine valley east of Lake Constance. The lords of Ems held castles above it in the Middle Ages, and it came under Habsburg rule in the late 14th century.

delft.s: Delft is a city in the province of South Holland, Netherlands, between Rotterdam and The Hague, which received town rights in 1246. It prospered from brewing, cloth and later the blue-and-white Delftware pottery.

dordrecht.s: Dordrecht is a city in South Holland, Netherlands, where several branches of the Rhine and Maas delta meet. Granted town rights in 1220, it is the oldest chartered town of Holland and long held staple rights over river trade.

dirk-i-count-of-holland.s: Dirk I (died c. 939) is regarded as the first Count of Holland.

darmstadt.s: Darmstadt is a city in southern Hesse, Germany, south of Frankfurt. It came to Hesse with the County of Katzenelnbogen in 1479 and was the capital of the landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt from 1567, of the Grand Duchy of Hesse from 1806 and of the People's State of Hesse until…

diessenhofen.s: Diessenhofen is a small town in the Swiss canton of Thurgau on the south bank of the Rhine, between Schaffhausen and Stein am Rhein. The counts of Kyburg granted it town rights in 1178; it then passed to the Habsburgs, and in 1460 the Swiss Confederates took it with the Thurgau.

detmold.s: Detmold is a city in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, at the edge of the Teutoburg Forest. It became the main residence of the rulers of Lippe, whose Renaissance palace still stands, and was the capital of the Principality and then the Free State of Lippe until 1947.

dillenburg.s: Dillenburg is a town in central Hesse, Germany, on the Dill. Its castle, built in the 13th century, became the main residence of the Ottonian counts of Nassau, and William the Silent was born there in 1533.

dillingen-an-der-donau.s: Dillingen an der Donau is a town in Bavarian Swabia, Germany, on the Danube. The seat of the counts of Dillingen, it passed to the bishops of Augsburg in 1258 and became their residence after they left their cathedral city.

dedition-of-nice-to-savoy.s: The Dedition of Nice to Savoy was the act of 1388 by which Nice and its hinterland, then part of the county of Provence, placed themselves under the protection of Amadeus VII, Count of Savoy. It followed the succession war after the death of Queen Joanna I, in which Nice…

douce-i-countess-of-provence.s: Douce I was Countess of Provence and heiress of its first comital dynasty. Her marriage to Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona in 1112 brought Provence to the counts of Barcelona, whose junior line ruled it until 1245.

davos.s: Davos is a town in the canton of Graubünden in eastern Switzerland, set in a high Alpine valley at about 1,560 metres. The League of the Ten Jurisdictions was formed there in 1436, and in the 19th century it became a health resort for tuberculosis patients, the setting of…

diane-de-poitiers.s: Diane de Poitiers was a French noblewoman and the mistress of King Henry II, who was nearly twenty years her junior. She held great influence at court and received many gifts, including the duchy of Valentinois and the château of Chenonceau, which Catherine de' Medici took…

diois.s: The Diois is a mountainous district in the Drôme department of south-eastern France, around the town of Die in the Drôme valley. In the Middle Ages it was a county disputed between the bishops of Die and the Poitiers counts of Valentinois, who joined it to their lands as the…

david-roentgen.s: David Roentgen was a German cabinetmaker who ran the family workshop at Neuwied founded by his father, Abraham Roentgen. Famous for pictorial marquetry and furniture with ingenious mechanisms, he sold to Marie Antoinette, Catherine the Great and other European courts and…

durham-castle.s: Durham Castle is a Norman castle in Durham, north-east England, begun in 1072 on the orders of William the Conqueror. For centuries it was the residence of the prince-bishops of Durham, who governed the county palatine from it.

durham-university.s: Durham University is a collegiate university in Durham, north-east England, founded by an act of Parliament in 1832 and granted a royal charter in 1837. It was endowed with property of the bishop and cathedral chapter of Durham, and the bishop's castle became its first college.

devlet-i-giray.s: Devlet I Giray was khan of Crimea from 1551 to 1577. A vassal and ally of the Ottoman Empire, he waged war on Muscovy, and in 1571 his army reached Moscow and burned much of the city.

democedes.s: Democedes of Croton was a Greek physician of the 6th century BCE. According to Herodotus he practised at Aegina, Athens and the court of Polycrates of Samos, was taken to Persia as a captive and cured King Darius I, then escaped home to Croton.

duncan-stewart-colonial-administrator.s: Sir Duncan Stewart was a British colonial administrator who became the second governor of the Crown Colony of Sarawak in 1949. Within weeks of his arrival he was stabbed by Rosli Dhobi, a member of the movement opposing Sarawak's cession to Britain, during a visit to Sibu in…

dabuya.s: Dabuya was a ruler in Tabaristan, northern Iran, in the 7th century, a son of Gil Gavbara and the figure from whom the Dabuyid dynasty took its name. According to the historian Ibn Isfandiyar his descendants ruled the lowlands of Tabaristan as ispahbads until the Abbasid…

downpatrick.s: Downpatrick is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland, near the south-western shore of Strangford Lough. Its early name, Dún Lethglaise, refers to the fort of the Dál Fiatach kings of the Ulaid, and tradition holds that Saint Patrick is buried at Down Cathedral.

domnall-mac-aedo.s: Domnall mac Áedo was a king of Cenél Conaill, a branch of the northern Uí Néill, and high king of Ireland, who died in 642. In 637 he defeated Congal Cáech of the Ulaid and his Dál Riata allies at the Battle of Mag Rath (Moira), one of the largest battles of early medieval…

dal-khalsa.s: The Dal Khalsa was the combined army of the Sikh misls, organised at Amritsar in 1748 under the overall command of Jassa Singh Ahluwalia. Its bands fought the Mughal governors of Punjab and the invasions of Ahmad Shah Durrani, with campaigns decided at gatherings of the Sarbat…

dunadd.s: Dunadd is a hillfort on a rocky outcrop in Kilmartin Glen, Argyll, in western Scotland. It was the main royal centre of the kingdom of Dál Riata from about the 6th to the 9th century, and excavations have found imported pottery, metalworking and fine jewellery.

dang-district.s: The Dang district is a hilly, forested district in southern Gujarat, India, bordering Maharashtra, with its headquarters at Ahwa. Known as the Dangs, it was long held by Bhil chiefs whose teak forests the British leased from the 1840s.

danishmendname.s: The Danishmendname is a Turkish epic about the deeds of Danishmend Gazi and his companions in their wars against the Byzantines in Anatolia. Based on oral tradition from the time of the Danishmendid emirate, it was reworked in Old Anatolian Turkish in 1360 by Arif Ali of Tokat…

daorson.s: Daorson was the fortified hilltop centre of the Illyrian Daorsi at Ošanići, near Stolac in Herzegovina. Its acropolis was enclosed by massive walls of large stone blocks, often compared with Mycenaean Cyclopean masonry, and finds include coins, helmets and Greek-style pottery…

durres.s: Durrës is a port city on the Adriatic coast of Albania, founded around 627 BCE by Greek colonists from Corinth and Corcyra under the name Epidamnos. The Romans called it Dyrrhachium and made it the starting point of the Via Egnatia to Thessalonica and Constantinople.

date-harumune.s: Date Harumune was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period and head of the Date clan of southern Mutsu. From 1542 he fought his father Date Tanemune in the Tenbun war, a conflict that drew in many neighbouring families; he won by 1548 and moved the clan's seat to Yonezawa.

datia-palace.s: The Datia Palace, also called the Bir Singh Palace, is a seven-storey palace on a rock above the town of Datia in Madhya Pradesh, India. It was built by the Bundela ruler Vir Singh Deo of Orchha in the early 17th century.

diomedes.s: Diomedes was a Greek hero of the Trojan War, king of Argos and one of the bravest fighters of the Iliad. Later legend told that on his return from Troy he sailed to southern Italy and founded Arpi and other towns in Daunia, northern Apulia.

dauphin-of-france.s: Dauphin of France was the title of the heir apparent to the French throne from 1350 to 1830. It derived from the Dauphins of Viennois, rulers of the Dauphiné, whose last count, Humbert II, sold his lands to France on condition that they pass to the king's eldest son.

dornoch-firth.s: The Dornoch Firth is a sea inlet on the east coast of the Scottish Highlands, dividing Easter Ross to the south from Sutherland to the north. The cathedral town of Dornoch stands on its northern shore.

denbighshire.s: Denbighshire is a county in north-east Wales, stretching from the coast at Rhyl and Prestatyn to the hills around Corwen, with its administrative centre at Ruthin. It includes much of the Vale of Clwyd and the Clwydian Range, and castles at Denbigh and Rhuddlan built during…

delminium.s: Delminium was the chief stronghold of the Delmatae, near modern Tomislavgrad in western Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Roman commander Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica destroyed it in 155 BCE, ending a war against the Delmatae.

dolaucothi-gold-mines.s: The Dolaucothi Gold Mines, near Pumsaint in Carmarthenshire, Wales, are the only Roman gold mines known in Britain. The Romans worked them from the late 1st century CE with open-cast pits, underground galleries and long aqueducts bringing water to wash the ore.

deogarh-odisha.s: Deogarh, also called Debagarh, is a town in western Odisha, India, the headquarters of Deogarh district. It was the capital of the princely state of Bamra, whose Raja Sudhal Deb set up a printing press there in the late 19th century that published Odia books and a newspaper,…

dobrotitsa.s: Dobrotitsa was the ruler of the Dobrujan principality on the western Black Sea coast from about 1347 until his death around 1386, with his seat at Kaliakra. The Byzantines gave him the title of despot.

dobruja.s: Dobruja is the region between the lower Danube and the Black Sea, divided between Romania in the north and Bulgaria in the south. In antiquity its coast was lined with Greek colonies such as Histria, Tomis and Callatis.

demetrios-palaiologos.s: Demetrios Palaiologos was a younger brother of the last Byzantine emperor, Constantine XI, and despot of the Morea from 1449 to 1460. After the fall of Constantinople he quarrelled and fought with his brother Thomas, who shared the despotate, and both faced Albanian revolts.

dewas.s: Dewas is a city in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, India, below a hill with a shrine of the goddess Chamunda. From the 1720s it was shared by two Maratha Puar states, Dewas Senior and Dewas Junior, whose rulers lived in separate palaces in the same town until 1948.

dinh-lien.s: Đinh Liễn was the eldest son of Đinh Tiên Hoàng, the first emperor of the Đinh dynasty of Đại Cồ Việt in Vietnam. He served his father as a commander and envoy, and the Song court gave him the title of prince of Giao Chỉ in the 970s.

droitwich-spa.s: Droitwich Spa is a town in Worcestershire, England, built over deposits of rock salt fed by natural brine springs. Salt was produced there in the Iron Age and Roman period, when the place was called Salinae, and in Anglo-Saxon times it was a major source of salt for the Hwicce…

dominican-liberation-party.s: The Dominican Liberation Party is a political party of the Dominican Republic, founded in 1973 by Juan Bosch after he left the Dominican Revolutionary Party. Under Leonel Fernández (1996–2000 and 2004–2012) and Danilo Medina (2012–2020) it held the presidency for most of two…

dol-de-bretagne.s: Dol-de-Bretagne is a town in north-eastern Brittany, France, near the Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel. By tradition it grew from a monastery founded by the Welsh saint Samson in the 6th century, and its bishops, from the 9th century until 1199, claimed to be archbishops of all Brittany.

douala.s: Douala is the largest city and main port of Cameroon, on the Wouri estuary near the Gulf of Guinea. It grew from the trading towns of the Duala people, whose chiefs dealt with European merchants from the 17th century, and became the centre of the German colony of Kamerun in 1884.

duala-people.s: The Duala are a Bantu-speaking people of the Cameroon coast, living mainly around the Wouri estuary and the city of Douala. From the 17th century their chiefs, notably the Bell and Akwa lineages, grew rich as middlemen in the Atlantic trade in slaves, ivory and palm oil.

drogo-of-hauteville.s: Drogo of Hauteville was a Norman adventurer who led the Normans of Apulia as count from 1046 until his murder in 1051. A son of Tancred of Hauteville, he came to southern Italy with his brother William Iron Arm and succeeded him, receiving investiture from Emperor Henry III in…

dusseldorf.s: Düsseldorf is the capital of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, on the Rhine. Count Adolf V of Berg granted it town rights in 1288 after the Battle of Worringen, and it became the residence of the counts and dukes of Berg and later of Elector Johann Wilhelm of the…

dankwarderode-castle.s: Dankwarderode Castle is a castle in the centre of Brunswick, Germany, built by Henry the Lion from about 1160 as his residence. In front of it stands the bronze Brunswick Lion, set up around 1166 as the symbol of his rule, beside the cathedral where he is buried.

dijon.s: Dijon is a city in eastern France and the historic capital of Burgundy. It was the seat of the Capetian dukes of Burgundy from the 11th century and of the Valois dukes from 1363, whose palace and tombs at the charterhouse of Champmol made it a centre of late Gothic art.

dukes-chair.s: The Duke's Chair is a double stone throne on the Zollfeld plain north of Klagenfurt in Carinthia, Austria, probably assembled in the 9th century from reused Roman stones. After their installation at the Prince's Stone, new dukes of Carinthia sat on it to receive homage and…

docibilis-i-of-gaeta.s: Docibilis I was the ruler of Gaeta from about 867 to about 906 and the founder of the dynasty that made the former Byzantine dependency a hereditary state. He allied at times with Arab raiders, allowing them to settle on the Garigliano, and grew rich from trade.

duchy-of-croatia.s: The Duchy of Croatia, also called Dalmatian or Littoral Croatia, was a medieval Slavic principality in the hinterland of the Dalmatian coast, formed in the late 8th and 9th centuries under Frankish and later Byzantine influence. Its rulers of the Trpimirović dynasty, such as…

drava.s: The Drava is a river of Central Europe, over 700 km long and a right tributary of the Danube. It rises in the Italian Alps, flows east through Carinthia in Austria and through Slovenia, and then forms much of the border between Croatia and Hungary before joining the Danube…

dagome-iudex.s: Dagome iudex is a summary, preserved in an 11th-century papal register, of a document from around 991 by which Duke Mieszko I of Poland, his wife Oda and their sons placed their land under the protection of the Holy See. It describes the boundaries of the state centred on…

doubravka-of-bohemia.s: Doubravka (d. 977) was a Bohemian princess, a daughter of Duke Boleslaus I, who married Mieszko I of Poland in 965.

darlowo.s: Darłowo (German: Rügenwalde) is a small town on the Baltic coast in the West Pomeranian Voivodeship of Poland, near the mouth of the Wieprza. Its castle was a residence of the Pomeranian dukes, and from 1449 King Eric of Pomerania, deposed from his Scandinavian thrones, lived…

diet-of-treptow.s: The Diet of Treptow was an assembly of the Pomeranian estates held at Treptow an der Rega (Trzebiatów) in December 1534, at which Dukes Barnim IX and Philip I introduced the Lutheran Reformation in Pomerania. The church order drawn up by Johannes Bugenhagen, himself a…

danevirke.s: The Danevirke is a system of earthwork defences across the base of the Jutland peninsula in Schleswig, now in northern Germany. Begun in the early Middle Ages and strengthened under King Godfred around 808 and by later kings, it guarded the southern frontier of Denmark and…

della-rovere.s: The della Rovere were a family from Savona in Liguria that rose through the Church. Francesco della Rovere became Pope Sixtus IV (1471–1484) and his nephew Giuliano became Pope Julius II (1503–1513).

dorothea-von-biron.s: Dorothea von Biron was the youngest daughter of Peter von Biron, Duke of Courland. She married Edmond de Talleyrand-Périgord, nephew of the French statesman Talleyrand, and became the elder Talleyrand's companion and hostess, notably at the Congress of Vienna and in London.

doclea.s: Doclea was a Roman town near present-day Podgorica in Montenegro, at the meeting of the Zeta and Morača rivers. Founded in the first century, it became the main city of the region and was later linked by tradition with the Emperor Diocletian.

dartmoor.s: Dartmoor is an upland area of granite moorland in Devon, south-west England, protected as a national park since 1951. It holds one of the densest concentrations of prehistoric remains in Britain, including stone rows, hut circles and Bronze Age field boundaries known as reaves.

devon.s: Devon is a county of south-west England, lying between Cornwall and Somerset with coasts on both the English Channel and the Bristol Channel. Its name comes from the Dumnonii, the Iron Age people of the peninsula, through the post-Roman kingdom of Dumnonia.

dorchester-dorset.s: Dorchester is the county town of Dorset in south-west England. It grew from Durnovaria, the Roman town that became the administrative centre of the Durotriges, close to the great Iron Age hillfort of Maiden Castle.

dorset.s: Dorset is a county on the English Channel coast of south-west England, with its county town at Dorchester. In the late Iron Age it was the heartland of the Durotriges, whose many hillforts include Maiden Castle and Hod Hill.

dharmachakra.s: The Dharmachakra, or Wheel of the Law, is a Buddhist symbol representing the teaching of the Buddha, recalling his first sermon at Sarnath, known as setting the wheel of the Dharma in motion. It is usually shown as a spoked wheel, often with eight spokes for the Eightfold Path.

durham-england.s: Durham is a city in north-east England on a loop of the River Wear. It was founded in 995 when the community of Saint Cuthbert settled there with his relics, and its Norman cathedral, begun in 1093, and castle together form a World Heritage Site.

desmond-rebellions.s: The Desmond Rebellions were two risings in Munster, in 1569 to 1573 and 1579 to 1583, led by the FitzGerald dynasty of Desmond and their allies against the expansion of English government under Elizabeth I. The second rebellion was crushed with great brutality and famine, and…

duong-van-nga.s: Duong Van Nga was a Vietnamese queen, wife of Dinh Bo Linh, founder of Dai Co Viet. After his murder in 979, as queen mother of the young king, she backed the general Le Hoan, who took the throne in 980 and defeated a Song invasion in 981.

daemusin-of-goguryeo.s: Daemusin was the third king of Goguryeo, reigning from 18 to 44 CE according to the Samguk sagi. He expanded the kingdom by war, invading Eastern Buyeo, whose king Daeso was killed in 22 CE, and attacking the Chinese commandery of Lelang.

daeso.s: Daeso was the last king of Eastern Buyeo, an early state in Manchuria, according to the Korean chronicle Samguk sagi. A son of Geumwa, he was a rival of Jumong, the founder of Goguryeo, and later fought Goguryeo.

dongmyeong-of-goguryeo.s: Dongmyeong, known as Jumong, was the founder of Goguryeo, traditionally in 37 BCE. Korean legend makes him the son of Yuhwa and a heavenly father, raised at the court of Eastern Buyeo, from which he fled south to found his kingdom at Jolbon in the Yalu valley.

draksharama.s: Draksharama is a temple town in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh, India, home to the Bhimeswara temple of Shiva, one of the five Pancharama shrines. The temple was built under the Eastern Chalukya kings of Vengi around the 9th and 10th centuries and carries hundreds of…

dyle.s: The Dyle (Dijle in Dutch) is a river in central Belgium, rising in Walloon Brabant and flowing north through Leuven and Mechelen to join the Nete and form the Rupel. In 891 Arnulf of Carinthia destroyed a Viking army on its banks near Leuven.

drumanagh.s: Drumanagh is a promontory fort on the coast of north County Dublin, near Loughshinny, enclosed by ditches across the neck of a headland. Finds of Roman coins and other objects of the 1st and 2nd centuries CE have made it the most debated evidence of Roman contact with Ireland,…

dublin.s: Dublin is the capital and largest city of Ireland, at the mouth of the River Liffey on the east coast. Founded as a Norse settlement in the 9th century, it became the centre of a Viking kingdom and, after the Anglo-Norman invasion of 1169–1171, the seat of English government…

dalta.s: Dalta was a king of Ellipi, a kingdom in the central Zagros mountains of western Iran, in the late 8th century BCE. A loyal vassal of the Assyrian king Sargon II, he was restored by Assyrian troops after a rebellion, and the rebels of Harhar turned to him against Assyria.

durand-line.s: The Durand Line is the border of about 2,640 kilometres between Afghanistan and Pakistan, fixed in an 1893 agreement between Emir Abdur Rahman Khan and Sir Mortimer Durand, foreign secretary of British India. It divided Pashtun and Baloch tribal lands between the two states,…

derbent.s: Derbent is a city in Dagestan, Russia, on a narrow strip of land between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus mountains. The Sasanians fortified the pass in the 6th century with long stone walls running from the sea into the hills, and the Arabs called it Bab al-Abwab, the Gate of…

diriyah.s: Diriyah is a town in Wadi Hanifa on the north-western edge of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It was the seat of the Al Saud and capital of the first Saudi state from the 18th century, where Muhammad ibn Saud allied with the preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in 1744.

dori.s: Dori is a town in north-eastern Burkina Faso, capital of the Sahel region. Around 1810 it became the capital of the Fulbe Emirate of Liptako, founded in the wake of Usman dan Fodio's jihad, and it was a market for livestock and trans-Saharan trade.

daman.s: Daman is a coastal town in western India, at the mouth of the Gulf of Khambhat. The Portuguese took it in 1559 and held it as part of the Estado da India for four centuries, building fortifications and churches.

demetrios-angelos-doukas.s: Demetrios Angelos Doukas was the last independent ruler of Thessalonica, a son of Theodore Komnenos Doukas. He succeeded his brother John in 1244 with the title of despot, but his unpopular rule alienated the city's nobles, who conspired with the emperor of Nicaea.

demetrios-chomatenos.s: Demetrios Chomatenos was archbishop of Ohrid from 1216 until the 1230s and a leading canon lawyer of the Orthodox Church, whose rulings survive in a large collection. Around 1227 he crowned Theodore Komnenos Doukas emperor at Thessalonica, defying the patriarch at Nicaea and…

dassaretae.s: The Dassaretae were an ancient people living around Lake Ohrid and the upper valleys to its west, in present-day North Macedonia and Albania. Ancient writers place them on the border between Illyria and Macedon, and their towns included Lychnidus.

drin.s: The Drin is the longest river of Albania. It is formed at Kukës by the junction of the Black Drin, which flows out of Lake Ohrid, and the White Drin, which rises in Kosovo, and it flows west through mountain gorges to the Adriatic.

dione.s: Dione was a Greek goddess worshipped with Zeus at the oracle of Dodona in Epirus, where she was his consort. In Homer she is the mother of Aphrodite.

dadusha.s: Dadusha was a king of Eshnunna in the Diyala region of Mesopotamia in the early 18th century BCE, the brother of Naram-Sin and son of Ipiq-Adad II. He made Eshnunna one of the great powers of the region alongside Shamshi-Adad I of Upper Mesopotamia.

dicuil.s: Dicuil was an Irish monk and scholar who worked at the Carolingian court in the early 9th century. Around 825 he wrote De mensura orbis terrae, a geographical survey of the world, in which he recorded that Irish hermits had lived on islands north of Britain, probably the…

dayton-agreement.s: The Dayton Agreement was the peace settlement that ended the Bosnian War, negotiated at an air base near Dayton, Ohio, in November 1995 and signed in Paris on 14 December 1995 by the presidents of Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. It kept Bosnia and Herzegovina as…

devlin-report.s: The Devlin Report was the report of a British commission of inquiry, chaired by the judge Patrick Devlin, into the state of emergency declared in Nyasaland in March 1959, when African nationalist leaders including Hastings Banda were arrested. Published in July 1959, it found…

domingo-de-monteverde.s: Domingo de Monteverde was a Spanish naval officer born in the Canary Islands who led the royalist reconquest of Venezuela in 1812. Advancing from Coro after the Caracas earthquake, he forced Francisco de Miranda to capitulate at San Mateo in July 1812, ending the First…

derby.s: Derby is a city in the East Midlands of England on the River Derwent. In the Viking Age it was one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw, taken by Æthelflæd of Mercia in 917.

dorbet.s: The Dörbet are a Mongolic people, one of the four main groups of the Oirat confederation of western Mongolia, together with the Choros, Torghut and Khoshut. Their ruling family was related to that of the Choros.

dole.s: Dole is a town on the Doubs in the Jura department of eastern France, formerly the capital of the Free County of Burgundy. It housed the county's parliament and, from 1422, its university.

daimler-motoren-gesellschaft.s: Daimler-Motoren-Gesellschaft was a German engine and car maker founded in 1890 by Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach at Cannstatt near Stuttgart. Its cars were sold under the name Mercedes from 1902, and in 1926 it merged with Benz & Cie to form Daimler-Benz.

dominique-de-gourgues.s: Dominique de Gourgues was a French soldier from Gascony. In 1568, to avenge the Spanish massacre of the Huguenot colonists of Fort Caroline in 1565, he led a privately financed expedition to Florida, where, with Timucua allies, he captured the Spanish forts on the St Johns…

devils-island.s: Devil's Island is the smallest of the three Îles du Salut off the coast of French Guiana. From 1852 to 1953 it formed part of France's penal colony and was used especially for political prisoners, among them Alfred Dreyfus, held there from 1895 to 1899.

description-de-legypte.s: The Description de l'Égypte is a large illustrated survey of ancient and modern Egypt and its natural history, compiled by the scholars who accompanied Napoleon Bonaparte's expedition of 1798–1801. Published by the French government in many volumes between 1809 and 1829, its…

duy-tan.s: Duy Tân was emperor of Vietnam of the Nguyễn dynasty from 1907 to 1916. Placed on the throne as a child after the French deposed his father Thành Thái, he grew opposed to French rule and in 1916 joined a planned uprising by Vietnamese troops.

destour.s: The Destour ('Constitution'), formally the Liberal Constitutional Party, was a Tunisian nationalist party founded in 1920 by Abdelaziz Thâalbi and others. It demanded a constitution and an elected assembly under the French protectorate, but its cautious leadership drew mainly…

dakar-niger-railway.s: The Dakar–Niger Railway is a line of about 1,290 km linking Dakar in Senegal with Koulikoro on the Niger River in Mali. Built in stages from the 1880s by joining the Kayes–Niger and Thiès–Kayes lines, it was completed in the early 1920s and became the main outlet for the…

dreyfus-affair.s: The Dreyfus Affair was a political scandal that divided France from 1894 to 1906. Captain Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish army officer, was wrongly convicted of spying for Germany, and the army covered up evidence pointing to Major Ferdinand Esterhazy. Émile Zola's open letter…

dorestad.s: Dorestad was an early medieval trading settlement near present-day Wijk bij Duurstede in the Netherlands, where the Rhine and the Lek divided. Between the 7th and 9th centuries it was one of the largest emporia of north-western Europe, controlled in turn by the Frisians and…

denis-rapontchombo.s: Denis Rapontchombo, born Antchouwé Kowe Rapontchombo and known to Europeans as King Denis, was a Mpongwe ruler on the south bank of the Gabon estuary. In 1839 he signed a treaty with the French naval officer Édouard Bouët-Willaumez granting France rights on part of the…

drynemeton.s: Drynemeton was the sacred meeting place of the Galatians in central Anatolia, recorded by the geographer Strabo. Its Celtic name is usually read as oak sanctuary.

dying-gaul.s: The Dying Gaul is an ancient marble statue of a wounded Celtic warrior, now in the Capitoline Museums in Rome. It is a Roman copy of a Hellenistic original, probably bronze, commissioned by Attalus I of Pergamon in the late 3rd century BCE to celebrate his victories over the…

drepung-monastery.s: Drepung Monastery, founded in 1416 by Jamyang Choje, a disciple of Tsongkhapa, lies on the outskirts of Lhasa in Tibet. It became the largest monastery of the Gelug school and once housed several thousand monks.

deutsche-handels-und-plantagen-gesellsch.s: The Deutsche Handels- und Plantagen-Gesellschaft der Südsee-Inseln zu Hamburg (DHPG) was a German trading and plantation company founded in 1878 to take over the Pacific business of the Hamburg firm J. C.

dromichaetes.s: Dromichaetes was a king of the Getae north of the lower Danube around 300 BCE. In about 292 BCE he defeated and captured Lysimachus, king of Thrace, who had invaded his land.

daeseong-dong-tumuli.s: The Daeseong-dong Tumuli are a cemetery of the 1st to 5th centuries CE in Gimhae, South Korea, regarded as the royal burial ground of Geumgwan Gaya. Excavations from 1990 uncovered wooden chamber tombs with iron armour, weapons, horse equipment and objects from Japan and…

dangun.s: Dangun is the legendary founder of Gojoseon, the first Korean kingdom. The thirteenth-century Samguk yusa describes him as the son of a heavenly prince and a bear transformed into a woman, and dates his founding of the state to 2333 BCE.

durlabhavardhana.s: Durlabhavardhana was the founder of the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir, ruling from about 625 to 661. According to Kalhana's Rajatarangini he succeeded the last Gonanda king through his marriage to the king's daughter.

daifang-commandery.s: Daifang was a Chinese commandery in north-western Korea, in the area of modern Hwanghae, carved out of Lelang by the warlord Gongsun Kang around 204. Later held by Wei and Jin, it was a centre of contact with the Han peoples of southern Korea and the Wa of Japan until pressure…

diaguita.s: The Diaguita were a group of indigenous peoples speaking the Cacán language who lived in the valleys of north-western Argentina and north-central Chile. Skilled farmers, potters and metalworkers, they came partly under Inca rule in the fifteenth century and fiercely resisted…

diet-of-porvoo.s: The Diet of Porvoo was the assembly of the four estates of Finland that met at Porvoo in 1809, during the Finnish War. Emperor Alexander I of Russia promised to uphold Finland's laws, Lutheran religion and privileges, and the estates swore allegiance to him as Grand Duke.

darmstadt-artists-colony.s: The Darmstadt Artists' Colony was founded in 1899 by Grand Duke Ernest Louis of Hesse on the Mathildenhöhe in Darmstadt to promote modern art and design. Its exhibition of 1901, with houses and studios by Joseph Maria Olbrich and Peter Behrens, was a landmark of Jugendstil,…

dakota-people.s: The Dakota are a Siouan-speaking Indigenous people, one of the main divisions of the Oceti Sakowin, or Seven Council Fires, often called the Sioux. The eastern Dakota, or Santee, lived around the upper Mississippi and Minnesota rivers, where they hunted, fished and gathered…

diodotus-i.s: Diodotus I was the Seleucid satrap of Bactria who broke away from the Seleucid Empire in the mid-3rd century BCE and founded the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom. His coins show him first striking in the name of the Seleucid king Antiochus II with his own portrait, then as king in his…

diodotus-ii.s: Diodotus II was the second king of the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, son and successor of Diodotus I, ruling in the later 3rd century BCE. He is reported to have made an alliance with the Parthian ruler Arsaces I against the Seleucids.

dickon-mitchell.s: Dickon Mitchell is a Grenadian lawyer and politician, leader of the National Democratic Congress. He became prime minister of Grenada in June 2022 after his party unexpectedly won the general election, defeating the New National Party of Keith Mitchell, which had governed for…

disentis-abbey.s: Disentis Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in the upper Rhine valley of Graubünden, Switzerland, founded in the early 8th century. Its abbots were powerful lords in the Surselva, and in 1395 the abbot joined local nobles and communes in the alliance that became the Grey League.

de-beers.s: De Beers is a diamond mining and trading company founded at Kimberley in South Africa in 1888, when Cecil Rhodes merged the mines of the area into De Beers Consolidated Mines with backing from the Rothschilds. For most of the 20th century it controlled the greater part of the…

diego-luis-de-san-vitores.s: Diego Luis de San Vitores was a Spanish Jesuit missionary who founded the first permanent Catholic mission in the Mariana Islands, landing on Guam in 1668. He named the islands after Queen Mariana of Austria and began the Spanish colonisation of Guam.

dunhuang.s: Dunhuang is an oasis city in the west of Gansu province, China, where the northern and southern Silk Road routes into the Tarim Basin divided. Founded as a Han dynasty garrison in the 2nd century BCE, it was a centre of trade and Buddhist culture, held by the Tibetan Empire…

diu.s: Diu is a town and island off the southern coast of the Saurashtra peninsula in Gujarat, India. A port of the Gujarat Sultanate, it was the scene of the naval Battle of Diu in 1509, and Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to build a fort there in 1535.

daulat-rao-scindia.s: Daulat Rao Scindia was the Maharaja of Gwalior from 1794 to 1827, successor of Mahadji Scindia as head of the Scindia family in the Maratha Confederacy. Defeated by the British at Assaye and Laswari in the Second Anglo-Maratha War, he ceded territory by the Treaty of…

diego-velazquez.s: Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter, court painter to Philip IV and a leading artist of the Spanish Golden Age. Born in Seville, he moved to Madrid in 1623 and painted portraits of the royal family, historical scenes such as The Surrender of Breda and the celebrated Las…

diyala-river.s: The Diyala is a river rising in the Zagros Mountains of western Iran, where it is called the Sirwan, and flowing through north-eastern Iraq to join the Tigris just south of Baghdad. Its valley was a main route between Mesopotamia and the Iranian plateau and was home to ancient…

diyar-rabia.s: Diyar Rabi'a, 'the abode of the Rabi'a', was the eastern province of the Jazira in upper Mesopotamia in early Islamic times, around Mosul, Nisibis and the upper Tigris. It took its name from the Arab tribes of the Rabi'a group, including the Banu Taghlib, who settled there…

dinavar.s: Dinavar was a medieval city in western Iran, north-east of Kermanshah, whose ruins lie near the modern village of the same name. Under the Abbasids it was a provincial centre of the Jibal and the home of scholars such as the polymath Abu Hanifa al-Dinawari.

divico.s: Divico was a leader of the Tigurini, a Helvetian people, who defeated a Roman army under Lucius Cassius Longinus near Agen in 107 BCE during the wars of the Cimbri. Julius Caesar records that, as an old man, he led the Helvetian embassy to Caesar in 58 BCE and defiantly…

dryopes.s: The Dryopes were an early people of Greece who, according to Greek tradition, first lived around Mount Oeta and Parnassus until they were driven out by Heracles and the Dorians. Their descendants were said to have settled at Hermione and Asine in the Peloponnese, at Karystos…

damghan.s: Damghan is a city in Semnan province, northern Iran, on the old road from Tehran to Khorasan. It holds the Tarikhaneh, one of the oldest surviving mosques in Iran.

debrecen.s: Debrecen is the second-largest city of Hungary, in the east of the country. A Calvinist centre since the 16th century, it served as the seat of the revolutionary government in 1849, when the Hungarian parliament proclaimed independence from the Habsburgs in its Great Reformed…

dengizich.s: Dengizich was a son of Attila who tried to restore Hun power after the empire broke up following his father's death in 453 and the defeat at the Nedao in 454. He campaigned against the Ostrogoths and in the late 460s attacked the Eastern Roman Empire on the lower Danube.

diagoras-of-rhodes.s: Diagoras of Rhodes was a celebrated boxer from Ialysos, whose victory at the Olympic Games of 464 BCE was praised by Pindar in his seventh Olympian ode. He also won at the other great Panhellenic games.

demetrius-of-pharos.s: Demetrius of Pharos was a Greek ruler of the Adriatic island of Pharos who served the Illyrian queen Teuta and then went over to Rome in the First Illyrian War of 229 BCE, receiving a domain on the coast. His later raids and alliance with Macedon provoked the Second Illyrian…

diocese-of-rottenburg-stuttgart.s: The Diocese of Rottenburg-Stuttgart is a Roman Catholic diocese covering the Württemberg part of the German state of Baden-Württemberg. It was created by papal bull in 1821 as the Diocese of Rottenburg for the Catholics of the enlarged Kingdom of Württemberg, many of whom…

dominikus-zimmermann.s: Dominikus Zimmermann was a German architect and stuccoist of the Bavarian rococo, born in Wessobrunn. Often working with his brother, the painter Johann Baptist Zimmermann, he built the pilgrimage church of Steinhausen from 1728 and the Wieskirche from 1745, a masterpiece of…

denizli.s: Denizli is a city in south-western Turkey, near the ruins of ancient Laodicea on the Lycus. The medieval Turkish town, known as Ladik, grew up nearby after Turkmen groups took the area in the late 13th century, and Ibn Battuta visited it around 1333, praising its…

douglas-hyde.s: Douglas Hyde was an Irish scholar of the Irish language and the first President of Ireland, from 1938 to 1945. In 1893 he co-founded the Gaelic League to revive the Irish language and culture, which inspired a generation of nationalists.

dail-eireann.s: Dáil Éireann is the lower house of the Irish parliament. It first met in Dublin on 21 January 1919, when Sinn Féin members elected in the 1918 general election declared Irish independence and formed the revolutionary assembly of the Irish Republic.

doha-agreement-2020.s: The Doha Agreement was signed on 29 February 2020 in Doha, Qatar, between the United States and the Taliban. The United States agreed to withdraw all its troops from Afghanistan within fourteen months, and the Taliban promised not to let al-Qaeda use Afghan territory and to…

douglas-isle-of-man.s: Douglas is the capital and largest town of the Isle of Man, on the island's east coast. It grew from a fishing port into a busy trading town and, in the 19th century, a popular seaside resort, and replaced Castletown as the seat of government in 1869.

durga.s: Durga is a major Hindu goddess, a warrior form of the divine mother who is celebrated for slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura. She is usually shown riding a lion or tiger and holding weapons in many arms.

dulha-rai.s: Dulha Rai is the ruler traditionally credited with founding Kachhwaha power in the Dhundhar region of eastern Rajasthan, in the 11th or 12th century. According to family chronicles he came from the Gwalior region, took territory from local Meena and Bargujar chiefs and set up…

defenders-of-the-homeland.s: The Defenders of the Homeland, known as PETA, was a volunteer army of Indonesians raised by the Japanese occupiers in Java in October 1943 to help resist an Allied invasion. Its units revolted at Blitar in February 1945.

dilip-singh-judeo.s: Dilip Singh Judeo was an Indian politician from the former royal family of Jashpur in Chhattisgarh. A leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party, he served in both houses of Parliament and as a minister of state in the national government in 2003.

daegu.s: Daegu is one of the largest cities of South Korea, in the south-east of the peninsula in the basin of the Nakdong river system. In ancient times it lay within the Jinhan confederacy and then Silla.

durgadas-rathore.s: Durgadas Rathore was a Rathore noble of Marwar who led resistance to the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb after the death of Maharaja Jaswant Singh in 1678. He protected the infant heir Ajit Singh and fought a long war until Ajit Singh regained Jodhpur in 1707.

donghak-peasant-revolution.s: The Donghak Peasant Revolution was a rising of Korean peasants in 1894, led by followers of the Donghak religion such as Jeon Bong-jun, against corruption, heavy taxes and foreign influence. When the Joseon court asked China for troops, Japan also sent forces, leading to the…

della-gherardesca.s: The della Gherardesca were a powerful noble family of Pisa, counts of Donoratico in Tuscany. After the fall of the Judicate of Cagliari in 1258 they received a third of its lands in south-western Sardinia, including the mining district around Iglesias.

dante-alighieri.s: Dante Alighieri was a Florentine poet and politician, author of the Divine Comedy. A White Guelph, he was exiled from Florence in 1302 and spent his remaining years at the courts of northern Italy, including Verona and Ravenna, where he died.

doria-family.s: The Doria were one of the great noble families of the Republic of Genoa, prominent from the 12th century. Doria admirals won victories over Pisa at Meloria in 1284 and Venice at Curzola in 1298, and the family held lands in northern Sardinia.

daylam.s: Daylam was the mountainous region south-west of the Caspian Sea, in the highlands of modern Gilan and Qazvin provinces of Iran. Its people, the Daylamites, long resisted Arab conquest.

daylamites.s: The Daylamites were an Iranian people of Daylam, the highlands south-west of the Caspian Sea, famed as tough infantry and mercenaries. They resisted Arab rule for centuries and adopted Islam in the 9th and 10th centuries, often in its Zaydi form, through Alid missionaries.

dexippus.s: Dexippus was an Athenian statesman and historian of the 3rd century. He is said to have led the defence of Athens against the Heruli in 267, and he wrote a chronicle of world history and the Scythica, an account of the Gothic wars.

dimapur.s: Dimapur is the largest city of Nagaland in north-east India, on the Dhansiri river. It was the capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom until the Ahoms sacked it in 1536.

dimasa-people.s: The Dimasa, also called Dimasa Kacharis, are a Tibeto-Burman people of north-east India, living mainly in the Dima Hasao, Karbi Anglong and Cachar districts of Assam and in Nagaland. They speak Dimasa, a Boro-Garo language, and are organised in clans.

dima-hasao.s: Dima Hasao, until 2010 called the North Cachar Hills, is a hill district of Assam, India, with its headquarters at Haflong. It is the homeland of the Dimasa people, whose kings ruled from Maibang in the 16th to 18th centuries.

dubkund.s: Dubkund is an archaeological site in northern Madhya Pradesh, India, which was the seat of a branch of the Kachchhapaghata dynasty in the 11th century. It is known for the ruins of a large Jain temple complex and for an inscription of 1088 recording the family's rulers and…

dargins.s: The Dargins, or Dargwa, are a Northeast Caucasian people of central Dagestan in the North Caucasus, speaking the Dargwa language. For centuries many lived in self-governing village communities and unions such as Akusha-Dargo, while others were subjects of the Kaitag utsmi.

danishnama-yi-alai.s: The Danishnama-yi Ala'i, "Book of Knowledge for Ala al-Dawla", is a philosophical encyclopaedia written in Persian by Ibn Sina (Avicenna) at Isfahan for his patron, the Kakuyid ruler Ala al-Dawla Muhammad. Covering logic, metaphysics and natural science, it is among the…

dinoyo-inscription.s: The Dinoyo inscription is a Sanskrit inscription of 760 found at Dinoyo near Malang in East Java, Indonesia, the earliest dated inscription from East Java. It records that King Gajayana of Kanjuruhan, son of Dewasimha, built a temple to the sage Agastya and replaced an old…

diogo-gomes.s: Diogo Gomes was a Portuguese navigator and explorer in the service of Prince Henry the Navigator. Around 1456 he sailed far up the Gambia River to the market of Cantor, in the kingdom of Kantora, where he learned of the gold trade of the interior.

derna.s: Derna is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Cyrenaica in eastern Libya. In 1805, during the First Barbary War, a small force of United States Marines and mercenaries led by William Eaton captured it from the Karamanli rulers of Tripoli, an action that helped bring about…

diocles-of-carystus.s: Diocles of Carystus was a Greek physician of the 4th century BCE from Karystos in Euboea, regarded in antiquity as second only to Hippocrates. Working in Athens, he wrote on anatomy, diet, hygiene and medicinal plants, and is credited with one of the first Greek herbals.

dur-kurigalzu.s: Dur-Kurigalzu was a royal city founded by the Kassite king Kurigalzu I in the early 14th century BCE, near modern Baghdad. It contained palaces and temples and a large ziggurat, whose mud-brick core still stands at Aqar Quf.

datu-pagbuaya.s: Datu Pagbuaya was a 16th-century chief of the Bohol coast in the central Philippines. According to Spanish accounts, after raiders from Ternate attacked Bohol around 1563 he led many survivors to the north coast of Mindanao, where they founded Dapitan.

datu-puti.s: Datu Puti is the leader of the ten Bornean datus in the Maragtas legend of the Visayas in the Philippines. According to the story he led them away from a tyrant in Borneo and bought the lowlands of Panay from the Ati chief Marikudo for a golden salakot and a gold necklace.

djanet.s: Djanet is an oasis town in south-eastern Algeria, at the foot of the Tassili n'Ajjer plateau. It was a centre of the Kel Ajjer Tuareg until French forces occupied it in 1911.

dharanidhar-naik.s: Dharanidhar Naik was a leader of the Bhuyan people of Keonjhar in Odisha, India, who led a revolt against the Raja of Keonjhar in 1891. The rising, known as the Dharanidhar Melli, protested against forced labour and other demands of the ruler and his officials.

devanagari.s: Devanagari is an Indian script, written from left to right with a characteristic horizontal headline, in which each consonant carries an inherent vowel. It developed from the Brahmi script through the Nagari scripts of northern India in the late first millennium CE.

david-soslan.s: David Soslan was an Alanian prince who became the second husband of Queen Tamar of Georgia around 1189 and her co-ruler. He commanded Georgian armies in victories over the Eldiguzids at Shamkor in 1195 and over the Seljuks of Rum at Basiani around 1202.

dordogne.s: Dordogne is a department of south-western France, in the region of Nouvelle-Aquitaine, roughly corresponding to the old province of Périgord, with its prefecture at Périgueux. It takes its name from the Dordogne river, which crosses it from east to west.

duncan-i-of-scotland.s: Duncan I was king of Scotland from 1034 to 1040, succeeding his maternal grandfather Malcolm II. His father was Crínán, abbot of Dunkeld.

dunkeld.s: Dunkeld is a small town on the River Tay in Perthshire, Scotland. In the 9th century Kenneth MacAlpin is said to have brought relics of St Columba there, and it became a leading church centre of the kingdom of Alba.

denpasar.s: Denpasar is the capital of the Indonesian province of Bali, in the south of the island. It grew around a palace built by the rulers of the Kingdom of Badung in the late 18th century, which became their leading court.

druk-gyalpo.s: Druk Gyalpo, 'Dragon King', is the title of the head of state of Bhutan. The hereditary monarchy was established in 1907, when an assembly at Punakha elected Ugyen Wangchuck as the first Druk Gyalpo, ending the old dual system of civil and religious rulers.

defenestration-of-prague-1618.s: The Defenestration of Prague took place on 23 May 1618, when Protestant nobles of Bohemia, angered by Habsburg restrictions on their religious rights, threw two Catholic regents and their secretary from a window of Prague Castle. All three survived the fall.

duleek.s: Duleek is a village in County Meath, Ireland, south-west of Drogheda. Its name comes from Damliag, 'stone church', and tradition makes it the site of one of the first stone churches in Ireland, founded by St Cianán in the 5th century.

derbforgaill.s: Derbforgaill was an Irish noblewoman, daughter of Murchad Ua Máel Sechlainn, king of Mide, and wife of Tigernán Ua Ruairc, king of Breifne. In 1152 she was carried off, apparently willingly, by Diarmait Mac Murchada of Leinster.

dioscurias.s: Dioscurias was an ancient Greek colony on the eastern shore of the Black Sea, founded by settlers from Miletus in the 6th century BCE on the site of modern Sukhumi in Abkhazia. It traded with the peoples of the Caucasus, and ancient writers claimed that dozens of languages…

dungarth.s: Dungarth was a king of Cornwall in the 9th century, whose drowning in 875 is recorded in the Annales Cambriae. He is usually identified with Doniert, named on a carved stone near St Cleer in east Cornwall that asks for prayers for his soul.

donnus.s: Donnus was a king of the Alpine peoples around Segusio (Susa) and the Montgenèvre pass in the 1st century BCE, in the time of Julius Caesar. He was the father of Marcus Julius Cottius, who made peace with Augustus and governed the region as a Roman prefect; the inscription on…

demonax-of-mantinea.s: Demonax of Mantinea was a Greek lawgiver invited to Cyrene around the middle of the 6th century BCE, on the advice of the Delphic oracle, to end civil strife there. He divided the citizens into three tribes and reduced the king's powers to religious duties and the royal estates.

decebalus.s: Decebalus was king of Dacia from 87 to 106 CE. He destroyed the Roman army of Cornelius Fuscus and in 89 CE won a favourable peace from Domitian, with Roman subsidies and engineers.

deceneus.s: Deceneus was a Dacian high priest and adviser to King Burebista in the 1st century BCE, according to Strabo and Jordanes. He is said to have helped Burebista unite the Dacians and to have persuaded them to cut down their vineyards and live soberly.

dagomba-people.s: The Dagomba, or Dagbamba, are a people of northern Ghana who speak Dagbani, a Gur language. Their kingdom, Dagbon, was founded by mounted invaders probably in the 15th century and is ruled by the Ya Na from Yendi.

daurama.s: Daurama is the queen of Daura in the Bayajidda legend, the origin story of the Hausa states. According to the legend she married the stranger Bayajidda after he killed the snake that guarded the Kusugu well, and their son Bawo fathered the founders of the seven Hausa kingdoms.

dawro-zone.s: The Dawro Zone is an administrative zone of south-western Ethiopia, between the Omo and Gojeb rivers, with its centre at Tarcha. It takes its name from the Dawro people and their former kingdom, conquered by Menelik II in 1891, and it contains the Halala Kella, a long…

derge-parkhang.s: The Derge Parkhang is a printing house and library in Dêgê, in the Kham region of eastern Tibet, founded in 1729 by King Tenpa Tsering of Derge. It holds hundreds of thousands of carved wooden blocks for the Buddhist canon and other Tibetan works, which are still used to print…

derge-gonchen-monastery.s: Derge Gonchen Monastery, also called Lhundrup Teng, is a Sakya monastery in Dêgê in Kham, eastern Tibet, founded in the 15th century. The royal family of Derge rose around it and made it their seat, and it stands beside the Derge Parkhang printing house founded by the kings in…

diawara.s: The Diawara are a Soninke clan of the western Sahel, found mainly in western Mali around Nioro and Kayes. According to their traditions they came to rule the kingdom of Diarra, replacing the Niakhate, and they remained a leading lineage of the region after the Bambara kingdom…

dipayal-silgadhi.s: Dipayal Silgadhi is a town in Doti district in far-western Nepal, on the Seti River. Dipayal was a seat of the Raika kings of Doti, and Silgadhi, the old town on the ridge above, was the trading centre of the region.

dommoc.s: Dommoc was the seat of the first bishopric of East Anglia, given around 630 by King Sigeberht to the Burgundian missionary Felix. It is traditionally identified with Dunwich on the Suffolk coast, though some historians favour the Roman fort at Walton near Felixstowe.

dunwich.s: Dunwich is a village on the Suffolk coast of England that in the Middle Ages was a major port and one of the largest towns in East Anglia. Storms from the late 13th century onwards and steady coastal erosion swept most of the town, including its churches, into the sea.

deidamia-ii-of-epirus.s: Deidamia was the last ruler of the Aeacid royal house of Epirus, a daughter of Pyrrhus II. She was killed during a revolt around 232 BCE, murdered in a temple of Artemis at Ambracia, after which the Epirotes abolished the monarchy and formed the Epirote League.

dodona.s: Dodona in Epirus, north-western Greece, was the oldest oracle of the Greek world, sacred to Zeus and Dione. Priests interpreted the rustling of a sacred oak, and enquirers wrote their questions on lead tablets, many of which survive.

dubricius.s: Dubricius, in Welsh Dyfrig, was a 6th-century British bishop and saint active in Ergyng, in south-east Wales and Herefordshire. Later tradition made him archbishop of Llandaff and the bishop who crowned King Arthur, but the earliest sources show him as a founder of churches in…

devenish-island.s: Devenish is an island in Lower Lough Erne, County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland, site of a monastery founded by Saint Molaise in the 6th century. Its remains include a fine 12th-century round tower, several churches and the Augustinian priory of St Mary.

deed-of-cession-fiji.s: The Deed of Cession was the instrument by which Ratu Seru Cakobau and other Fijian chiefs ceded Fiji to Queen Victoria on 10 October 1874, making the islands a British colony. Signed at Levuka, it followed the collapse of Cakobau's settler-dominated government under debt.

diego-gelmirez.s: Diego Gelmírez was bishop and from 1120 the first archbishop of Santiago de Compostela, and the most powerful churchman in Galicia. He rebuilt the cathedral, promoted the pilgrimage to the tomb of Saint James and took a leading part in the politics of Queen Urraca's reign and…

drohiczyn.s: Drohiczyn is a small town on the Bug River in eastern Poland, once an important stronghold on the borders of Rus', Poland and Lithuania. In 1253 Daniel of Galicia was crowned King of Rus' there by a papal legate.

dalem-waturenggong.s: Dalem Waturenggong was king of Gelgel in Bali in the 16th century, under whom the kingdom reached its height. His realm included Bali, Lombok, Blambangan in eastern Java and parts of Sumbawa, and his court received the Javanese priest Dang Hyang Nirartha, who reshaped Balinese…

dang-hyang-nirartha.s: Dang Hyang Nirartha was a Shaivite priest from Java who came to Bali in the 16th century, during the reign of Dalem Waturenggong of Gelgel. He reformed Balinese Hinduism, introducing the padmasana shrine to the supreme god, and is credited with founding sea temples such as…

debre-markos.s: Debre Markos is a town in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia, in the highlands of Gojjam south of Lake Tana. Founded in the mid-19th century as a royal centre, it was the capital of the kings and governors of Gojjam.
