desmond-tutu.s: Desmond Tutu was a South African Anglican cleric and anti-apartheid campaigner, Archbishop of Cape Town from 1986 to 1996. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984 for his non-violent opposition to apartheid.

domini-di-terraferma.s: The Domini di Terraferma were the mainland territories of the Republic of Venice in northern Italy, conquered mainly between 1339 and 1428 and including Treviso, Padua, Vicenza, Verona, Brescia and Bergamo, with Friuli. They kept their own statutes and councils under Venetian…

democratic-republic-of-yemen.s: The Democratic Republic of Yemen was a breakaway state proclaimed in Aden on 21 May 1994 by Ali Salim al-Beidh, the former leader of South Yemen, during the civil war that followed unification. It controlled much of the former south but won no international recognition, and it…

danse-macabre-notke.s: The Danse Macabre by Bernt Notke is a painting on canvas showing figures of every rank, from pope and emperor downwards, being led away by dancing skeletons. Made for St Nicholas' Church in Reval (Tallinn) in the late 15th century, it survives as a fragment about 7.5 metres…

derbyshire.s: Derbyshire is a county in the East Midlands of England, including much of the Peak District. Its lead deposits were mined in Roman times, when lead pigs stamped with the name of the district were produced, and mining continued through the Middle Ages.

domitius-domitianus.s: Lucius Domitius Domitianus was a usurper who proclaimed himself emperor in Egypt in 297, probably in reaction to Diocletian's tax reforms. Coins were struck in his name at Alexandria, and the corrector Aurelius Achilleus supported him.

dioscorus-i-of-alexandria.s: Dioscorus I was Patriarch of Alexandria from 444 to 451. He presided over the Second Council of Ephesus in 449, which restored the monk Eutyches, but the Council of Chalcedon in 451 deposed and exiled him.

declaration-of-state-sovereignty-of-the-.n: Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Russian SFSR
declaration-of-state-sovereignty-of-the-.s: The Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Russian SFSR was adopted by the republic's Congress of People's Deputies on 12 June 1990. It proclaimed the supremacy of Russia's constitution and laws over those of the Soviet Union, strengthening Boris Yeltsin against the Union…

drangiana.s: Drangiana was an ancient region in the basin of the Helmand river and Lake Hamun, on the borders of modern Iran and Afghanistan. It was a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire and was crossed by Alexander the Great in 330 BCE.

delos.s: Delos is a small island in the Cyclades, revered in antiquity as the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis and one of the greatest sanctuaries of the Greek world. It held the treasury of the Delian League from 478 BCE, and in the second century BCE, as a free port under Roman…

duris-of-samos.s: Duris of Samos was a Greek historian and tyrant of his native island in the early third century BCE. He wrote histories of Macedon and Greece from 370 BCE, a history of Agathocles of Syracuse and works on Samos, all now lost except in fragments.

domitian.s: Domitian was Roman emperor from 81 to 96 CE, the last of the Flavian dynasty. He strengthened the Danube frontier, fought wars against the Dacians, the Chatti and the Sarmatian Iazyges, and carried out a large building programme in Rome.

don-river.s: The Don is a river of south-western Russia, about 1,870 kilometres long, flowing from south of Moscow to the Sea of Azov. Known to the Greeks as the Tanais, it was regarded in antiquity as the boundary between Europe and Asia and between the Scythians and the Sarmatians.

dhanyakataka.s: Dhanyakataka was an ancient city on the Krishna river in present-day Andhra Pradesh, India, at modern Dharanikota beside Amaravati. In the second century CE it became a capital of the later Satavahana kings, and the nearby Amaravati stupa grew into a great centre of Buddhist art.

daji.s: Daji was the favourite consort of Di Xin, last king of the Shang dynasty, in traditional Chinese histories. Later writers portrayed her as a cruel woman whose influence led the king into tyranny and brought about the fall of the dynasty, and the Ming novel Investiture of the…

di-yi.s: Di Yi was the penultimate king of the Shang dynasty and father of Di Xin, the last Shang king. Oracle-bone inscriptions of his reign show a strict, regular schedule of sacrifices to the royal ancestors and campaigns against the Renfang, peoples to the east of the Shang heartland.

dhaid.s: Dhaid is an oasis town in the interior of the emirate of Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, about 50 kilometres east of Sharjah city. Watered by underground channels, it was long known for its date palms and farms, and served as a meeting place for Bedouin tribes.

divine-bell-of-king-seongdeok.s: The Divine Bell of King Seongdeok is a large bronze bell of Silla, begun by King Gyeongdeok in memory of his father Seongdeok and completed in 771 under King Hyegong. It weighs about 19 tonnes and is decorated with flying celestial figures.

do-muoi.s: Do Muoi was a Vietnamese communist leader who served as prime minister from 1988 to 1991 and as general secretary of the Communist Party from 1991 to 1997. He continued the Doi Moi market reforms while keeping the party's monopoly of power, and during his leadership Vietnam…

dmitri-shostakovich.s: Dmitri Shostakovich was a Russian composer, among the most important of the twentieth century, best known for his fifteen symphonies and fifteen string quartets. His opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District was denounced in Pravda in 1936, and he was attacked again in 1948,…

daodejing.s: The Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) is the founding text of Daoism, a short collection of about 81 sections of verse traditionally attributed to the sage Laozi. It teaches that the Dao, the nameless source of all things, works through non-action and yielding, and it advises rulers to…

duke-hui-of-jin.s: Duke Hui of Jin, personal name Yiwu, ruled the Chinese state of Jin from 650 to 637 BCE. He gained the throne with support from Duke Mu of Qin but broke his promises of land and refused Qin grain during a famine.

duke-jing-of-qin.s: Duke Jing of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 576 to 537 BCE. His tomb near Fengxiang in Shaanxi, the ancient Qin capital Yong, was excavated between 1976 and 1986 and is the largest pre-imperial tomb found in China.

duke-wen-of-qin.s: Duke Wen of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 765 to 716 BCE. He defeated the Rong peoples and took the lands around Mount Qi, the old Zhou heartland in the Wei valley, gathering the Zhou population that remained there.

duke-wu-of-qin.s: Duke Wu of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 697 to 678 BCE. According to the Shiji, in 688 BCE he turned conquered territory at Gui and Ji into counties (xian) governed directly by the ruler, among the earliest known in China.

duke-xian-of-qin.s: Duke Xian of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 384 to 362 BCE. On his accession he banned the custom of burying people with their dead lords, and he moved the capital east to Yueyang.

duke-xiang-of-qin.s: Duke Xiang of Qin ruled the Qin people from 777 to 766 BCE. In 770 BCE, after the sack of the western Zhou capital, he escorted King Ping of Zhou eastward to Luoyi.

duke-xiao-of-qin.s: Duke Xiao of Qin ruled the State of Qin from 361 to 338 BCE. Determined to recover the lands lost to Wei, he invited able men from other states and appointed Shang Yang, whose reforms reorganised Qin around agriculture, war, strict law and counties under central control.

dobrzyn-land.s: Dobrzyń Land is a historical region of central Poland on the right bank of the Vistula, north-east of Płock. A frontier land between Masovia, Kuyavia and Prussia, it was repeatedly contested between Poland and the Teutonic Order, which held it from 1329 until the Treaty of…

duchy-of-prussia.s: The Duchy of Prussia was the state created in 1525 when Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach, the last Grand Master in Prussia, secularised the Teutonic Order's lands and became their hereditary duke under Polish overlordship. It was the first state to adopt Lutheranism officially.

dorylaeum.s: Dorylaeum was an ancient and Byzantine city in Phrygia, north-western Anatolia, on the site of present-day Eskişehir in Turkey. Lying on the main road from Constantinople into central Anatolia, it was a frequent military base and battlefield.

danishmendids.s: The Danishmendids were a Turkmen dynasty that ruled north-central and north-eastern Anatolia, from cities such as Sivas, Tokat, Niksar and Malatya, from the late eleventh century. Founded by Danishmend Gazi, they captured Bohemond of Antioch in 1100 and were at first stronger…

dada.s: Dada was an avant-garde art movement founded in 1916 at the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich by artists who had taken refuge in neutral Switzerland during the First World War. Rejecting reason and bourgeois art, which they blamed for the war, its members, among them Hugo Ball,…

diamond-sutra-of-dunhuang.s: The Diamond Sutra of Dunhuang is a Chinese woodblock-printed copy of the Diamond Sutra, a Mahayana Buddhist scripture, dated to 868 in the Tang dynasty. Found in 1900 in the sealed library cave of the Mogao Caves near Dunhuang and acquired by Aurel Stein in 1907, it is the…

democratic-party-uganda.s: The Democratic Party is a Ugandan political party founded in 1954, which drew much of its support from Catholics, particularly in Buganda. Its leader Benedicto Kiwanuka headed the government under internal self-government in 1961–1962, but it lost the pre-independence election…

daniel-oconnell.s: Daniel O'Connell was an Irish political leader known as the Liberator. His Catholic Association organised mass, peaceful pressure that forced the British government to grant Catholic emancipation in 1829, and he then led a campaign for repeal of the Act of Union, which…

david-ricardo.s: David Ricardo was a British political economist and one of the leading classical economists. His Principles of Political Economy and Taxation (1817) developed the theory of comparative advantage, the labour theory of value and the law of diminishing returns; he made a fortune…

democratic-republican-party.s: The Democratic-Republican Party was an American political party founded in the early 1790s by Thomas Jefferson and James Madison in opposition to Alexander Hamilton's Federalists. Favouring states' rights, agrarian interests and a strict reading of the Constitution, it held…

delcy-rodriguez.s: Delcy Rodríguez is a Venezuelan lawyer and politician of the United Socialist Party of Venezuela, the daughter of the left-wing leader Jorge Antonio Rodríguez. She served as foreign minister, presided over the Constituent Assembly of 2017 and became vice-president under…

deva-raya-i.s: Deva Raya I was emperor of Vijayanagara of the Sangama dynasty from 1406 to 1422. Early in his reign he was defeated by Firuz Shah Bahmani and had to make peace on unfavourable terms, but he later recovered ground against the Bahmani Sultanate.

deva-raya-ii.s: Deva Raya II was emperor of Vijayanagara of the Sangama dynasty from 1424 to 1446, under whom the empire reached a high point. He reformed the army, recruiting Muslim cavalry and archers, fought the Bahmani Sultanate and the Gajapatis of Odisha, and received the Persian envoy…

domingo-paes.s: Domingo Paes was a Portuguese traveller and horse trader who visited the Vijayanagara Empire around 1520, during the reign of Krishnadevaraya. His detailed account of the capital, its palaces, markets and temples and the Mahanavami festival, is one of the main sources for the…

dmitry-of-pereslavl.s: Dmitry of Pereslavl (Dmitry Alexandrovich) was the second son of Alexander Nevsky, prince of Pereslavl-Zalessky and grand prince of Vladimir for most of the period from 1276 to 1293. His rivalry with his brother Andrei of Gorodets set the khans of the Golden Horde against…

dudenevs-raid.s: Dudenev's raid was a punitive campaign by an army of the Golden Horde under the commander Dudenev (Duden), sent by Tokhta Khan in 1293 at the request of Andrei of Gorodets against his brother, Grand Prince Dmitry of Pereslavl. The army sacked Vladimir, Suzdal, Moscow, Kolomna…

dambal.s: Dambal is a village in Gadag district, Karnataka, India, known for the Doddabasappa temple, a twelfth-century Western Chalukya temple with an unusual star-shaped plan of twenty-four points. Inscriptions show that in the Western Chalukya period it also had a Buddhist monastery,…

durgasimha.s: Durgasimha was a Kannada poet and minister of the Western Chalukya king Jayasimha II in the early eleventh century. His Panchatantra, adapted from Sanskrit sources in the champu style of mixed verse and prose, is one of the earliest versions of the Panchatantra fables in a…

duoyou-ding.s: The Duoyou ding is a Western Zhou bronze cauldron, found in 1980 near Xi'an, whose inscription of nearly 280 characters records a campaign against the Xianyun in the late ninth century BCE. It describes a series of battles, the numbers of enemies killed and captured and of…

dugu-xin.s: Dugu Xin was a Xianbei general of the Western Wei dynasty and one of its Eight Pillars of State. His daughters married into three imperial houses: one became empress of the Northern Zhou, another, Dugu Qieluo, was empress of the Sui founder Emperor Wen, and a third was the…

dukuza.s: Dukuza was the royal capital built by the Zulu king Shaka around 1827 near the coast north of Port Natal, in what is now KwaZulu-Natal. Shaka was assassinated there in September 1828 by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana.

dhammayangyi-temple.s: The Dhammayangyi Temple is the largest temple at Bagan in Myanmar, built around 1170 by King Narathu of the Pagan Kingdom, who according to tradition seized the throne by murdering his father and brother. Its massive brickwork is admired for its precise construction, while its…

dato-bahaman.s: Dato Bahaman was a Malay chief of the Semantan district of Pahang who led the Pahang uprising against British rule from 1891 to 1895. Resenting the loss of his traditional rights under the British resident, he fought with Mat Kilau and other chiefs in a guerrilla war until the…

devapala-pala-emperor.s: Devapala was emperor of the Pala dynasty of Bengal and Bihar in the first half of the 9th century, the son of Dharmapala. His inscriptions claim wide conquests, and under him Pala power was at its height.

draupadi.s: Draupadi is the heroine of the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata, daughter of King Drupada of Panchala and the common wife of the five Pandava brothers. Her humiliation in the Kaurava court, after Yudhishthira lost her in a game of dice, is one of the epic's central episodes and a…

demeter.s: Demeter was the Greek goddess of grain, agriculture and the fertility of the earth, and mother of Persephone. The myth of Persephone's abduction by Hades and Demeter's search for her explained the cycle of the seasons and lay at the heart of the Eleusinian Mysteries, the most…

didda.s: Didda was the ruler of Kashmir from 980 to 1003, after governing as regent for her son and grandsons from 958. A princess of Lohara and wife of King Kshemagupta of the Parvagupta dynasty, she outlasted rivals through intrigue and had several young kings removed.

daud-al-fatani.s: Daud al-Fatani was a Malay Islamic scholar from Pattani who spent most of his life in Mecca, where he taught and wrote. He produced dozens of works in Malay, written in Jawi script, on law, theology and Sufism, which were widely used in religious schools across the Malay world.

divrigi.s: Divriği is a town in Sivas province in eastern Turkey, near the upper Euphrates. As Tephrike it was the fortified capital of the Paulicians in the 9th century until the Byzantines took it around 878.

demetrios-ypsilantis.s: Demetrios Ypsilantis was a Greek army officer of the War of Independence from a Phanariot family; his brother Alexandros led the rising of 1821 in the Danubian Principalities. Arriving in the Peloponnese in June 1821 as his brother's representative, he claimed the national…

dimitrov-constitution.s: The Dimitrov Constitution was the constitution of the People's Republic of Bulgaria adopted on 4 December 1947 and named after the communist leader Georgi Dimitrov. Modelled on the Soviet constitution of 1936, it proclaimed Bulgaria a people's republic, provided for the…

deng-xiaoping.s: Deng Xiaoping was a Chinese communist revolutionary who was the paramount leader of the People's Republic of China from 1978 until the early 1990s. Purged twice during the Cultural Revolution, he returned after Mao's death and launched the policy of reform and opening,…

dvin.s: Dvin was an ancient city of Armenia on the Ararat plain, south of modern Yerevan. Founded as a royal residence in the 4th century, it became the seat of the Sasanian marzpans, of the Armenian catholicos and later of the Arab governors of Arminiya.

densatil.s: Densatil was a Tibetan Buddhist monastery in the Lhoka region of central Tibet, founded in 1158 by Phagmo Drupa Dorje Gyalpo, a disciple of Gampopa. It became the mother monastery of the Phagdru Kagyu school and the spiritual centre of the Phagmodrupa rulers, who built richly…

daochus-ii.s: Daochus II was a nobleman of Pharsalus in Thessaly who served Philip II of Macedon as tetrarch of Thessaly and represented the Thessalians on the Amphictyonic Council at Delphi. Around 336–332 BCE he set up at Delphi a group of marble statues of his family, the Daochus…

drakensberg.s: The Drakensberg is the highest mountain range of southern Africa, forming the eastern escarpment of the Great Escarpment along the border of South Africa and Lesotho. It rises to 3,482 metres at Thabana Ntlenyana in Lesotho.

dionysius-of-phocaea.s: Dionysius of Phocaea was a Greek naval commander during the Ionian Revolt against Persia. Before the Battle of Lade in 494 BCE the Ionian fleet put him in charge of its training, though Herodotus says the crews soon tired of his hard drill.

dumnacus.s: Dumnacus was a leader of the Andecavi, a Gallic people of the lower Loire around Angers. During the last revolts against Julius Caesar in 51 BCE he besieged Duratius, the pro-Roman chief of the Pictones, in Lemonum (Poitiers).

duratius.s: Duratius was a leader of the Pictones, a Gallic people of the lower Loire and Poitou, who remained loyal to Rome during the Gallic revolts against Julius Caesar. In 51 BCE he was besieged in Lemonum (Poitiers) by Dumnacus of the Andecavi until Roman forces relieved him.

drweca.s: The Drwęca is a river of northern Poland, about 207 kilometres long, a right tributary of the Vistula, which it joins near Toruń. For much of the Middle Ages its lower course marked the border between the Kulmerland of the Teutonic Order and the Polish lands of Dobrzyń.

dili.s: Dili is the capital and largest city of East Timor, on the north coast of the island of Timor. The Portuguese moved their colonial capital there from Lifau in 1769, and it remained the seat of Portuguese Timor until 1975.

diocese-of-bolzano-brixen.s: The Diocese of Bolzano-Brixen is the Catholic diocese of South Tyrol in northern Italy. It continues the bishopric of Säben and Brixen, whose bishops were also princes of the Holy Roman Empire until 1803, and took its present form in 1964, when the see moved to Bolzano and its…

diocese-of-dresden-meissen.s: The Diocese of Dresden-Meissen is the Catholic diocese of Saxony, Germany, with its seat at Dresden. It continues the bishopric of Meissen, founded in 968, whose Catholic remnant survived the Reformation in Upper Lusatia under the dean of Bautzen.

donaustauf.s: Donaustauf is a market town on the Danube east of Regensburg in Bavaria, Germany. Its castle belonged to the bishops of Regensburg, and above it stands the Walhalla, a hall of fame of German history built for King Ludwig I between 1830 and 1842.

damian-hugo-philipp-von-schonborn.s: Damian Hugo Philipp von Schönborn was a German churchman of the powerful Schönborn family, made a cardinal in 1715. As prince-bishop of Speyer from 1719, he moved the bishops' residence from Philippsburg to Bruchsal and built the baroque palace there.

deventer.s: Deventer is a city on the IJssel in the Dutch province of Overijssel and one of the oldest towns in the Netherlands, founded around a church built by the missionary Lebuinus in the 8th century. It grew rich as a Hanseatic trading town under the bishops of Utrecht.

drenthe.s: Drenthe is a province in the north-east of the Netherlands, with Assen as its capital. A thinly settled land of heath and peat, it is known for its prehistoric megalithic tombs, the hunebedden.

dessau.s: Dessau is a city in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, where the Mulde joins the Elbe. It was the residence of the princes of Anhalt-Dessau from 1603 and the capital of the united Duchy of Anhalt from 1863.

dessau-worlitz-garden-realm.s: The Dessau-Wörlitz Garden Realm is a group of landscape parks laid out in the late 18th century around Dessau by Prince Leopold III Friedrich Franz of Anhalt-Dessau and his architect Friedrich Wilhelm von Erdmannsdorff. Inspired by English gardens, it combined parks, palaces…

donika-kastrioti.s: Donika Kastrioti, born Andronika Arianiti, was the daughter of the Albanian nobleman Gjergj Arianiti and the wife of Skanderbeg, whom she married in 1451. The marriage bound the powerful Arianiti family to Skanderbeg's cause.

deister.s: The Deister is a wooded ridge in Lower Saxony, Germany, south-west of Hanover, rising to about 405 metres. Running north-west to south-east between the Weser hills and the Leine valley, it formed the western edge of the medieval territory of Calenberg.

dictionnaire-de-trevoux.s: The Dictionnaire de Trévoux was a French dictionary and encyclopaedia first published in 1704 at Trévoux, in the Dombes, by Jesuit scholars. Based on the dictionary of Antoine Furetière, it was expanded in many editions up to 1771, the last in eight volumes.

donaueschingen.s: Donaueschingen is a town in the Black Forest-Baar district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, at the meeting of the Brigach and Breg, which form the Danube. From the 18th century it was the residence of the princes of Fürstenberg, whose palace park contains a spring regarded as…

drino.s: The Drino is a river of north-western Greece and southern Albania, rising in Greek Epirus and flowing north-west past Gjirokastër to join the Vjosë near Tepelenë. Its broad valley was a farming corridor and a route between Epirus and central Albania, and in the late 14th…

diber.s: Dibër is a mountainous region of eastern Albania along the Black Drin, bordering North Macedonia. Historically it formed a wider district, Dibra, centred on the town of Debar, which now lies in North Macedonia.

dragos-voivode-of-moldavia.s: Dragoș was a Romanian noble from Maramureș who, according to tradition, was sent by King Louis I of Hungary around 1346–1347 to found a frontier march on the Moldova river against the Golden Horde. Remembered as the first voivode of Moldavia, he was followed by his son and…

dmitry-shemyaka.s: Dmitry Yuryevich Shemyaka was a Russian prince of Galich, son of Yury of Zvenigorod, and a leading figure in the civil war over the throne of Moscow. He seized Moscow in 1446 and had his cousin Vasily II blinded, but was driven out within a year.

diez.s: Diez is a small town on the Lahn in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. Seat of the medieval counts of Diez, it passed to the House of Nassau and from 1606 was the residence of the counts, later princes, of Nassau-Diez, ancestors of the Dutch royal house.

divashtich.s: Divashtich was the ruler of Panjikent in Sogdiana who in the early 720s claimed the titles king of Sogdiana and lord of Samarkand. Resisting the Umayyad Arab conquest, he retreated to the castle on Mount Mugh, where he was captured in 722 and crucified.

demir-kapija.s: Demir Kapija, Turkish for 'iron gate', is a gorge of the Vardar river and a small town at its mouth in south-eastern North Macedonia. The narrow defile was a strategic point on the route from the Aegean to the central Balkans, guarded in the Middle Ages by the fortress of Prosek.

dmitrov.s: Dmitrov is a town in Moscow Oblast, Russia, about 65 kilometres north of Moscow. It was founded in 1154 by Yuri Dolgoruky, who named it after the patron saint of his newborn son Vsevolod, baptised Dmitry.

dmitry-bobrok-volynsky.s: Dmitry Bobrok-Volynsky was a Russian commander of the 14th century, a nobleman from Volhynia who entered the service of Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow. At the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380 he and Prince Vladimir the Bold of Serpukhov led the hidden ambush regiment, whose…

dmitry-pozharsky.s: Prince Dmitry Pozharsky was a Russian nobleman and commander. During the Time of Troubles he led, with the Nizhny Novgorod merchant Kuzma Minin, the national militia that drove the Polish garrison out of Moscow in 1612, opening the way for the election of Michael Romanov as tsar.

dmitry-of-uglich.s: Dmitry of Uglich was the youngest son of Ivan the Terrible. After his father's death he lived with his mother at Uglich, where in 1591 he died of a knife wound to the throat.

dolwyddelan-castle.s: Dolwyddelan Castle is a native Welsh castle in Snowdonia, built in the early 13th century by Llywelyn the Great to guard a route through the mountains of Gwynedd. Its stone keep is typical of the castles of the Welsh princes.

dover-new-hampshire.s: Dover is a city in south-eastern New Hampshire, United States, on the Cochecho River near the Piscataqua. Settled from about 1623 as a fishing station, it is the oldest permanent settlement in New Hampshire.

dukes-laws.s: The Duke's Laws were the legal code issued in 1665 for the territories of James, Duke of York, after the English capture of New Netherland. Drawn up under Governor Richard Nicolls and first applied on Long Island, they allowed Protestant congregations to choose their own…

delaware-river.s: The Delaware River flows about 480 km from the Catskill Mountains to Delaware Bay, forming parts of the borders of New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware. In the 17th century the Dutch, the Swedes of New Sweden and the English competed for its fur trade, and William…

dominican-restoration-war.s: The Dominican Restoration War was a guerrilla war fought from 1863 to 1865 against Spain's reannexation of the Dominican Republic. It began with the Grito de Capotillo on 16 August 1863, and the rebels set up a provisional government at Santiago, with leaders such as Gregorio…

darwin-northern-territory.s: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory, on the Timor Sea. Founded by South Australia in 1869 as Palmerston, it became the northern end of the Overland Telegraph in 1872 and was officially renamed after Charles Darwin in 1911.

dumat-al-jandal.s: Dumat al-Jandal is an ancient oasis town in the Jawf region of northern Saudi Arabia, at the head of the Wadi Sirhan. Known to the Assyrians as Adummatu, it was the centre of the Qedarite Arabs and the shrine of their gods, whose images Sennacherib carried off in the 7th…

dikwa.s: Dikwa is a town in Borno State, north-eastern Nigeria, south of Lake Chad. The Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr made it his capital after conquering Bornu in 1893.

devarakonda.s: Devarakonda is a town in Nalgonda district, Telangana, India, overlooked by a hill fort of the same name. In the 14th and 15th centuries the fort was a stronghold of the Recherla Nayakas, the Velama chiefs who ruled Telangana after the fall of the Kakatiyas, alongside their…

dominador-gomez.s: Dominador Gómez was a Filipino physician, labour leader and politician who headed the Unión Obrera Democrática, one of the first Filipino labour federations, from 1903. In 1906 he acted as intermediary between the American authorities and the guerrilla leader Macario Sakay,…

domodossola.s: Domodossola is a town in Piedmont, northern Italy, the main centre of the Val d'Ossola near the Swiss border, on the road and railway from Milan to the Simplon Pass. From 10 September to October 1944 it was the capital of the Partisan Republic of Ossola, one of the free zones…

dagobert-of-pisa.s: Dagobert of Pisa, also called Daimbert, was Archbishop of Pisa and the first Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem. Sent as papal legate, he led a Pisan fleet to the Holy Land during the First Crusade and was elected patriarch at the end of 1099.

duccio.s: Duccio di Buoninsegna was the founder of the Sienese school of painting, active from the 1270s. His Maestà, a huge double-sided altarpiece of the Virgin and Child, was carried in procession to Siena Cathedral in 1311.

dp-world.s: DP World is a multinational port and logistics company based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, formed in 2005 by merging the Dubai Ports Authority and Dubai Ports International. It operates container terminals on six continents, among them Jebel Ali in Dubai.

dorsland-trek.s: The Dorsland Trek ('Thirstland Trek') was a series of migrations by Boer families from the Transvaal across the Kalahari region between 1874 and 1881, seeking land and freedom from British influence. Many people and cattle died of thirst and disease on the way through…

draza-mihailovic.s: Draža Mihailović was a Yugoslav army officer who led the royalist Chetnik movement in occupied Yugoslavia during the Second World War and served as minister of war of the government-in-exile. After brief cooperation with Tito's Partisans in 1941 his forces fought them, and…

dositej-obradovic.s: Dositej Obradović was a Serbian writer, translator and Enlightenment thinker who promoted writing in the vernacular Serbian language rather than Church Slavonic. After decades of travel and study across Europe, he joined the First Serbian Uprising and became the first minister…

daik.s: Daik is a town on Lingga Island in the Riau Islands of Indonesia. From the late 18th century it was the seat of the sultans of Johor-Riau and later of the Riau-Lingga Sultanate, while the Bugis viceroys governed from Penyengat.

deed-of-surrender.s: The Deed of Surrender was the agreement of 1869 by which the Hudson's Bay Company surrendered its charter rights over Rupert's Land to the British Crown, for transfer to the Dominion of Canada, in return for 300,000 pounds, land around its posts and a share of the fertile…

draa-river.s: The Draa is the longest river of Morocco, rising in the High Atlas and flowing south-east and then west to the Atlantic, though its lower course is usually dry. Its middle valley is a long chain of palm oases and fortified villages on the edge of the Sahara.

drikung-kagyu.s: The Drikung Kagyu is a school of the Kagyu tradition of Tibetan Buddhism, founded in 1179 by Jigten Sumgön at Drikung Thil monastery north-east of Lhasa. In the 13th century the Drikung sought Mongol patronage in rivalry with the Sakya, and their revolt was crushed by Yuan and…

dora-baltea.s: The Dora Baltea is a river of north-western Italy that rises below Mont Blanc and flows through the Aosta Valley and past Ivrea to join the Po. In antiquity the Salassi worked gold deposits in its valley by washing, and quarrels with Roman contractors over its water led to war.

dharanikota.s: Dharanikota is a village on the Krishna river in the Guntur region of Andhra Pradesh, India, close to the great Buddhist stupa of Amaravati. It is identified with ancient Dhanyakataka, a fortified town that served as a capital of the later Satavahana kings in the eastern Deccan.

dammam.s: Dammam is a city on the Persian Gulf coast of Saudi Arabia and the capital of its Eastern Province. In 1938 the well Dammam No.

diophantes.s: Diophantes, son of Asclepiodorus, was a general from Sinope in the service of Mithridates VI of Pontus. Around 110–107 BCE he led campaigns in the Crimea to defend Chersonesus against the Scythian king Palakus and his Roxolani allies, and he put down the revolt of Saumacus in…

decree-of-aristoteles.s: The Decree of Aristoteles is an Athenian inscription of 378/377 BCE, proposed by a certain Aristoteles, that sets out the founding terms of the Second Athenian League. It invites Greeks and non-Greeks not ruled by the Persian king to join an alliance so that the Spartans may…

daeng-chelak.s: Daeng Chelak was one of five Bugis brothers from Sulawesi who won great influence in the Malay world in the early 18th century. He served as Yang Dipertuan Muda, or viceroy, of the Johor-Riau Sultanate and fought on its behalf across the Strait of Malacca.

duqaq.s: Duqaq was the Seljuk ruler of Damascus from 1095 to 1104, a son of Tutush I. His rivalry with his brother Ridwan of Aleppo left Syria divided when the First Crusade arrived.

dulat-tribe.s: The Dulat are one of the largest tribes of the Senior Jüz of the Kazakhs, living mainly in the Zhetysu region of south-eastern Kazakhstan. Traditionally nomadic herders, they were closely linked with the oasis cities of the Syr Darya.

doubs.s: The Doubs is a river of eastern France and western Switzerland, about 450 km long and a tributary of the Saône. It forms part of the Franco-Swiss border and winds in a tight loop around the city of Besançon, the ancient Vesontio.

dusans-code.s: Dušan's Code was the law code of the Serbian Empire, adopted by Stefan Dušan at an assembly in Skopje in 1349 and enlarged in 1354. It set out the rights of the Church, the nobility and the peasantry and drew on Byzantine law.

dnyaneshwar.s: Dnyaneshwar was a Marathi poet-saint who in 1290 completed the Dnyaneshwari, a verse commentary on the Bhagavad Gita and one of the founding works of Marathi literature. A key figure of the Varkari devotional movement, he is said to have entered samadhi at Alandi at the age of…

dra-abu-el-naga.s: Dra' Abu el-Naga is a necropolis on the west bank of the Nile at Thebes, opposite modern Luxor. It holds the tombs of kings of the Seventeenth Dynasty and early Eighteenth Dynasty, buried beneath small pyramids, as well as many tombs of officials.

desna-river.s: The Desna is a river of Russia and Ukraine, about 1,130 km long, which joins the Dnieper just above Kyiv. Bryansk, Novhorod-Siverskyi and Chernihiv stand on its banks.

darab.s: Darab is a city in the east of Fars province in southern Iran. Its predecessor Darabgerd, a circular walled city of Sasanian times, was one of the main cities of Fars, and nearby rock reliefs commemorate early Sasanian kings.

du-yuesheng.s: Du Yuesheng was a Shanghai gangster who rose to lead the Green Gang and became one of the most powerful men in the city between the world wars. Based in the French Concession, he controlled the opium trade and gambling, and in 1927 his men helped Chiang Kai-shek crush the…

dubai-creek.s: Dubai Creek is a saltwater inlet that divides Dubai into Deira and Bur Dubai. The Al Bu Falasah settled on its banks in 1833, and its sheltered harbour made Dubai a centre of pearling and trade with Iran and India.

doha.s: Doha is the capital and largest city of Qatar, on the east coast of the Qatar peninsula. A small pearling settlement in the 19th century, it became the seat of the Al Thani family, whose leader Muhammad bin Thani signed an agreement with Britain there in 1868.

dukhan.s: Dukhan is a town on the west coast of Qatar and the centre of the country's main onshore oil field. Oil was found there in 1939, and after delays caused by the Second World War exports began in 1949, giving Qatar the revenues that funded its modern development.

deng-ai.s: Deng Ai was a general of the state of Cao Wei in the Three Kingdoms period of China. After years defending the western frontier against Shu Han, in 263 he led a force over the mountains by a dangerous route to the Chengdu plain, and Liu Shan surrendered, ending Shu.

devabhuti.s: Devabhuti was the last king of the Shunga dynasty of northern India. The Puranas and Bana's Harshacharita record that around 73 BCE he was killed at the instigation of his Brahmin minister Vasudeva Kanva, who seized the throne and founded the Kanva dynasty.

ducetius.s: Ducetius was a leader of the Sicels, the native people of eastern Sicily, who around 460 BCE united most Sicel communities in a league against the Greek cities. He founded new towns, took Morgantina and challenged Syracuse and Acragas, but was defeated in 450 BCE and exiled to…

diogenes-the-cynic.s: Diogenes the Cynic (c. 412–323 BCE) was a Greek philosopher born in Sinope on the Black Sea, and the best-known figure of the Cynic school.

doon-valley.s: The Doon Valley is a wide valley in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, lying between the Sivalik Hills and the Lesser Himalaya and bounded by the Ganges and Yamuna rivers. Its main city, Dehradun, is the state capital.

doi-moi.s: Đổi Mới ('renovation') is the programme of economic reform adopted by the Sixth Congress of the Communist Party of Vietnam in December 1986. It returned farming to households, legalised private business, freed most prices and opened the country to foreign investment and trade…

daleminzia.s: Daleminzia, or Glomaci, was a Slavic tribal territory on the middle Elbe around Lommatzsch in present-day Saxony, inhabited by a Sorbian tribe. In 929 the East Frankish king Henry the Fowler stormed its stronghold of Gana and founded the castle of Meissen nearby, bringing the…

dance-of-zalongo.s: The Dance of Zalongo is the name given to the mass suicide of Souliote women on Mount Zalongo in Epirus in December 1803, after Ali Pasha of Ioannina had forced Souli to surrender. According to tradition, the women, to avoid capture by his troops, threw their children and then…

dakhla.s: Dakhla is a city on a long peninsula on the Atlantic coast of Western Sahara. Spain founded it in 1884 as Villa Cisneros, a trading post and fort, and it became the capital of the colony of Río de Oro.

dingtao-district.s: Dingtao is a district of Heze in south-western Shandong province, China. In antiquity the area around it, then called Taoqiu or Tao, was the capital region of the State of Cao and later a famous trading city where Fan Li, the minister of Yue, is said to have grown rich.

duke-zhuang-of-zheng.s: Duke Zhuang of Zheng (reigned 743–701 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Zheng who made it the leading state of the early Spring and Autumn period. He defeated a revolt by his younger brother Gongshu Duan and quarrelled with the Zhou court, where he had served as a minister.

diretorio-dos-indios.s: The Diretório dos Índios was a Portuguese law of 1757, drawn up by Governor Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado and extended to all Brazil in 1758, that ended missionary control over the indigenous villages of Amazonia. The villages became Portuguese-style towns under lay…

directorate-of-ukraine.s: The Directorate of Ukraine was the collective revolutionary government of the Ukrainian People's Republic, formed in November 1918 to overthrow Hetman Pavlo Skoropadsky's German-backed Ukrainian State. Led first by Volodymyr Vynnychenko and from 1919 by Symon Petliura, it took…

duke-wen-of-teng.s: Duke Wen of Teng was ruler of the small State of Teng in south-western Shandong in the late 4th century BCE. He sought the advice of the philosopher Mencius on mourning rites and good government, and Mencius urged him to restore the well-field system of land allotment.

duke-of-shao.s: The Duke of Shao, personal name Ji Shi, was a senior member of the Zhou royal house who helped King Wu overthrow the Shang. With the Duke of Zhou he served as a regent and leading minister under the young King Cheng, and he was enfeoffed with the northern State of Yan, which…

domoni.s: Domoni is a town on the east coast of Anjouan in the Comoros. It was the early capital of the Anjouan sultanate founded by Shirazi-descended rulers around 1500, and it keeps old stone houses, mosques and tombs, though the ruling house later moved to Mutsamudu.

dan-kassawa.s: Dan Kassawa was a leader of the Hausa ruling family of Katsina who, after the Fulani jihad of Usman dan Fodio drove them from Katsina, led the exiles to Maradi in the early 19th century. There, around 1819, he founded a state that claimed to continue the old Katsina Kingdom,…

dzaoudzi.s: Dzaoudzi is a town on Petite-Terre, a small island off the east coast of Mayotte in the Comoros archipelago. It became the seat of the sultans of Mayotte, and after France took possession of Mayotte in 1843 it was fortified as the French administrative centre.

dezhou.s: Dezhou is a city in north-western Shandong province, China, on the Grand Canal. In 1417 Paduka Batara, one of the rulers of Sulu who led a mission to the Ming court of the Yongle Emperor, died there on his journey home and was buried with imperial honours.

dyah-pitaloka.s: Dyah Pitaloka was a princess of the Sunda Kingdom, daughter of King Linggabuana. In 1357 she travelled to Majapahit to marry King Hayam Wuruk, but when the chief minister Gajah Mada demanded that she be handed over as a sign of Sunda's submission, the Sundanese party was…

dhul-nunid-dynasty.s: The Dhul-Nunid dynasty (Banu Dhi al-Nun) was a Berber family that ruled the Taifa of Toledo from the 1030s to 1085. From their lordships of Uclés and Huete they were invited to Toledo, where Ismail al-Zafir founded the dynasty.

denia.s: Dénia is a port town on the Mediterranean coast of the province of Alicante, Spain. In the 11th century it was the capital of the maritime taifa of Mujahid al-Amiri, which ruled the Balearic Islands, raided Sardinia and was known for Quranic scholarship.

dushanbe.s: Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan, on the Varzob river in the Hisor valley. A market village named after its Monday bazaar, it was chosen as capital of the Tajik ASSR in 1924 and grew rapidly as a planned Soviet city.

donald-cameron-colonial-administrator.s: Sir Donald Charles Cameron (1872–1948) was a British colonial administrator who served as governor of Tanganyika Territory from 1925 to 1931 and of Nigeria from 1931 to 1935. In Tanganyika he introduced indirect rule through chiefs and native authorities, modelled on Lugard's…

dodoma.s: Dodoma is the official capital of Tanzania, in the centre of the country. A small town on the Central Railway built under German rule, it was designated the new capital in 1973, but government offices moved there only slowly, mostly after 2016.

dungan-people.s: The Dungans are Chinese-speaking Muslims; the name is used in Central Asia for the Hui people of north-western China. After the failure of the great Muslim revolt against Qing rule of 1862–1877, many fled into the Russian Empire, where their descendants live in Kyrgyzstan and…

dax.s: Dax is a spa town on the Adour in the Landes department of south-western France. As Aquae Tarbellicae it was the chief town of the Aquitanian Tarbelli and became famous under Rome for its hot springs, still used for thermal cures.

demaratus-of-corinth.s: Demaratus of Corinth was, according to Roman tradition, a nobleman of the Bacchiad family who fled Corinth in the 7th century BCE and settled at the Etruscan city of Tarquinii. There he married a local woman, and his son Lucumo moved to Rome and became its fifth king,…

dora-riparia.s: The Dora Riparia is an Alpine river of north-western Italy that rises near the Montgenèvre Pass and flows east through the Susa Valley to join the Po at Turin. Its valley carried one of the main routes across the western Alps into the Po plain, used since antiquity.

diocese-of-turku.s: The Diocese of Turku is the oldest diocese in Finland, established in the 13th century, with its seat at Turku from about 1300. Under Swedish rule it covered all of Finland, and its cathedral and bishops, among them the reformer Mikael Agricola, shaped the country's church and…

democratic-party-united-states.s: The Democratic Party is one of the two major political parties of the United States, organised in the 1820s around supporters of Andrew Jackson and descended from Thomas Jefferson's Democratic-Republicans. It contested elections against the Whigs and, from the 1850s, the…

dinguiraye.s: Dinguiraye is a town in north-eastern Guinea, on the edge of the Futa Jallon highlands. In 1849 the Tijani scholar Umar Tall established a fortified base there, where he trained followers and gathered firearms before launching in 1852 the jihad that created the Toucouleur Empire.

drome.s: The Drôme is a department of south-eastern France, named after the Drôme river, a tributary of the Rhône, with its capital at Valence. It extends from the Rhône valley into the pre-Alps of the Vercors and the Diois.

donnuban-mac-cathail.s: Donnubán mac Cathail was king of the Uí Fidgenti, in what is now County Limerick, in the later 10th century. Allied with Ivar, the Norse king of Limerick, he took part in the capture of Mathgamain, king of Munster, who was handed over to his enemies and killed in 976.

duke-adolf-friedrich-of-mecklenburg.s: Adolf Friedrich of Mecklenburg was a German prince, explorer and colonial governor. He led a scientific expedition across central Africa in 1907–1908 and was governor of German Togoland from 1912 to 1914.

declaration-of-the-independence-of-new-z.n: Declaration of the Independence of New Zealand
declaration-of-the-independence-of-new-z.s: The Declaration of the Independence of New Zealand, in Māori He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni, was signed at Waitangi on 28 October 1835 by 34 northern Māori chiefs, organised by the British Resident James Busby. It declared New Zealand an independent state…

dhvanyaloka.s: The Dhvanyaloka ('Light on Suggestion') is a Sanskrit treatise on poetics by the Kashmiri critic Anandavardhana, written in the 9th century under the Utpala dynasty. It argues that suggestion (dhvani) and the evocation of emotional states (rasa) are the soul of poetry.

dzata.s: Dzata is the site of the stone-walled capital of the Venda kingdom in the Nzhelele valley of Limpopo province, South Africa, traditionally founded by the Singo dynasty after it crossed the Limpopo around 1700. Its ruins, with dressed-stone walls in a tradition linked to Great…

decimus-junius-brutus-albinus.s: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus was a Roman general and one of Julius Caesar's leading officers in Gaul, where in 56 BCE he commanded the fleet that destroyed the navy of the Veneti. Although favoured by Caesar, he joined the conspiracy against him and took part in his…

duchy-of-nemours.s: The duchy of Nemours was a French duchy-peerage centred on the town of Nemours, south of Paris, created in 1404 when Charles III of Navarre gave up the county of Évreux and other lands to Charles VI. It passed through several houses, including Armagnac, Foix and Savoy,…

dormition-cathedral-vladimir.s: The Dormition Cathedral in Vladimir, Russia, was built of white limestone in 1158–1160 by Andrei Bogolyubsky and enlarged after a fire in the 1180s by Vsevolod the Big Nest. It was the mother church of north-eastern Rus', and in 1238 the grand prince's family died in it when…

die-drome.s: Die is a small town in the Drôme valley in south-eastern France. As Dea Augusta it replaced Luc-en-Diois under the Roman Empire as one of the chief towns of the Vocontii, and it later became the seat of a bishopric; parts of its Roman walls and a monumental gate survive.

diploma-andreanum.s: The Diploma Andreanum was a charter issued by King Andrew II of Hungary in 1224 granting collective privileges to the German 'guests', the Transylvanian Saxons, settled around Hermannstadt (Sibiu). It gave them their own count, judges and freely elected priests, freedom of…

dummers-war.s: Dummer's War, also called Father Rale's War, was fought in 1722–1725 between New England and the Wabanaki Confederacy, supported by New France, over English settlement in what is now Maine and Nova Scotia. A New England raid destroyed the Abenaki village of Norridgewock in…

dom-domingos-of-warri.s: Dom Domingos was an Olu, or king, of the Itsekiri kingdom of Warri in the Niger Delta in the early 17th century. Raised as a Catholic under the influence of Portuguese missionaries, he spent several years in Portugal and around 1600 married a Portuguese woman.

darod.s: The Darod are one of the major clan families of the Somali people, tracing descent from the ancestor Abdirahman bin Isma'il al-Jabarti, known as Darod. They live across north-eastern and southern Somalia, the Somali Region of Ethiopia and north-eastern Kenya.

dromahair.s: Dromahair is a village in County Leitrim, Ireland, on the River Bonet near Lough Gill. It was the main seat of the O'Rourke lords of Breifne and later West Breifne, and in 1152 it was the scene of the abduction of Derbforgaill, wife of Tigernán Ua Ruairc, by Diarmait Mac…

detroit.s: Detroit is a city in Michigan, United States, on the Detroit River between Lake Erie and Lake Huron. It was founded in 1701 by Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac as Fort Pontchartrain du Détroit, a French fur-trading post, and passed to Britain in 1760.

durvinita.s: Durvinita was a king of the Western Ganga dynasty of southern Karnataka in the 6th century, often regarded as the most notable of its early rulers. He enlarged the Ganga kingdom in wars with neighbouring powers.

dhaun-castle.s: Dhaun Castle, Schloss Dhaun, is a castle above the Simmerbach valley near Hochstetten-Dhaun in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, first recorded in the early 13th century. It was a seat of the Wildgraves and then of the Wild- and Rhinegraves, giving its name to the line of…

denhardt-brothers.s: Clemens and Gustav Denhardt were German brothers who explored the Tana River region of East Africa in the 1870s. In 1885 they negotiated a treaty with Ahmad Simba, sultan of Witu, that placed his territory under German protection as German Witu, or Wituland.

dong-chang.s: Dong Chang (died 896) was a late Tang warlord who controlled Yuezhou, in modern Zhejiang, as military governor. In 895 he proclaimed himself emperor of a state called Luoping, but the Tang court ordered his former subordinate Qian Liu to suppress him, and Qian Liu's forces…

dmytro-vyshnevetsky.s: Dmytro Vyshnevetsky, remembered in Ukrainian folk song as Baida, was a Ruthenian prince and Cossack leader. Around 1552 he built a fort on the island of Mala Khortytsia on the Dnieper, often regarded as the forerunner of the Zaporozhian Sich, and led campaigns against the…

durad-ii-balsic.s: Đurađ II Balšić, son of Stracimir and so also called Stracimirović, was lord of Zeta from 1385 to 1403. Caught between the Ottomans, whose overlordship he accepted, and Venice, he handed Skadar and other towns to Venice in 1396.

druk-desi.s: The Druk Desi was the civil ruler of Bhutan under the dual system of government created by Ngawang Namgyal, the Zhabdrung, in the seventeenth century, while the Je Khenpo headed the monastic body. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the office was often fought over by…

dooars.s: The Dooars are the alluvial plains along the southern foot of the eastern Himalayas, in present-day West Bengal and Assam, India, which control the passes into Bhutan. Bhutan held them until the Duar War of 1864 to 1865, after which the Treaty of Sinchula ceded them to British…

dingling.s: The Dingling were an ancient people of the steppes south of Lake Baikal, recorded in Chinese sources from the third century BCE, when they were subdued by the Xiongnu. Many later settled in northern China, and in the late fourth century the Dingling Zhai clan founded the…

dazexiang-uprising.s: The Dazexiang uprising was the first major revolt against the Qin dynasty, begun in 209 BCE by Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, leaders of a party of conscripts held up by rain at Dazexiang in present-day Anhui. Facing death for arriving late, they rebelled, and Chen Sheng proclaimed…

dong-zhuo.s: Dong Zhuo was a Chinese general and warlord of the late Han dynasty. Called to the capital Luoyang in 189 during a court crisis, he seized power, deposed the young emperor in favour of Emperor Xian and ruled through terror.

dominican-war-of-independence.s: The Dominican War of Independence was the war by which the Dominican Republic won its independence from Haiti, which had ruled the whole of Hispaniola since 1822. Independence was proclaimed in Santo Domingo on 27 February 1844, and Dominican forces repelled a series of…

dutch-portuguese-war.s: The Dutch–Portuguese War was a largely colonial conflict fought from 1598 to 1663 between the Dutch Republic and the Portuguese Empire, which shared its king with Spain until 1640. The Dutch East and West India Companies seized Portuguese bases in Asia, including Malacca…

dzungar-qing-wars.s: The Dzungar–Qing Wars were a series of conflicts from 1687 to 1757 between the Qing dynasty of China and the Dzungar Khanate of the western Mongols. Begun by Galdan's attack on the Khalkha Mongols, they extended to Tibet and Central Asia and ended with the Qing conquest of…

danish-hanseatic-war-1361-1370.s: The Danish–Hanseatic War of 1361–1370 was fought between Valdemar IV of Denmark and the Hanseatic towns after Valdemar captured Visby on Gotland in 1361. After an early Danish victory, the Hanseatic Confederation of Cologne and its allies defeated Denmark in a second war from…

dutch-hanseatic-war.s: The Dutch–Hanseatic War was a naval and trade war from 1438 to 1441 between the Wendish towns of the Hanseatic League, led by Lübeck, and the towns of Holland and Zeeland, which were challenging Hanseatic control of the Baltic trade. Privateers on both sides attacked shipping.

dodecanese-campaign.s: The Dodecanese campaign was a British attempt in late 1943 to seize the Italian-held Dodecanese islands in the Aegean after Italy's armistice with the Allies. British forces landed on Kos, Leros and Samos, but Rhodes stayed in German hands.
